L7@P1: BACKGROUND
L8@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to using responsibly sourced raw materials including the
L9@P1: use of products derived from animals. This policy forms part of our commitment to uphold
L10@P1: the M&S animal welfare principles for all animal derived products we source.
L11@P1: SCOPE
L12@P1: This policy covers products sold in all Clothing, Home and Beauty areas that contain any
L13@P1: animal derived raw materials. The scope includes all main fabrics/textiles, trims,
L14@P1: componentry packaging, chemicals, pigments and dyestuffs.
L15@P1: This policy is intended to complement the additional specific sourcing policies for
L16@P1: Cashmere, Wool, Leather and Feather and Down.
L17@P1: RATONALE AND OBJECTIVES
L18@P1: • To ensure Marks & Spencer meets its long-standing commitment to improve animal
L19@P1: welfare in its supply chains and ensure all animal derived materials are sourced from
L20@P1: farms with good animal welfare practices. Marks & Spencer are committed to
L21@P1: improving animal welfare across our global supply chains and we are working to
L22@P1: source all animal-derived materials from farms with good animal welfare practices
L23@P1: • To lay out a set of uniform principles and guidelines around the sourcing of animal
L24@P1: derived raw materials
L25@P1: • To also ensure that appropriate due diligence is undertaken with regards to the
L26@P1: sourcing of products in relation to animal welfare
L27@P1: M&S MANDATORY PRINCIPLES FOR SOURCING
L28@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to protecting any endangered or vulnerable species and

L4@P0-1: ANIMAL WELFARE POLICYLatest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L5@P1: Version Number 2.0 Page 2 of 5
L6@P1: Public Copy
L7@P1: BACKGROUND
L8@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to using responsibly sourced raw materials including the
L9@P1: use of products derived from animals. This policy forms part of our commitment to uphold
L10@P1: the M&S animal welfare principles for all animal derived products we source.
L11@P1: SCOPE
L12@P1: This policy covers products sold in all Clothing, Home and Beauty areas that contain any
L13@P1: animal derived raw materials. The scope includes all main fabrics/textiles, trims,
L14@P1: componentry packaging, chemicals, pigments and dyestuffs.
L15@P1: This policy is intended to complement the additional specific sourcing policies for
L16@P1: Cashmere, Wool, Leather and Feather and Down.
L17@P1: RATONALE AND OBJECTIVES
L18@P1: • To ensure Marks & Spencer meets its long-standing commitment to improve animal
L19@P1: welfare in its supply chains and ensure all animal derived materials are sourced from
L20@P1: farms with good animal welfare practices. Marks & Spencer are committed to
L21@P1: improving animal welfare across our global supply chains and we are working to
L22@P1: source all animal-derived materials from farms with good animal welfare practices
L23@P1: • To lay out a set of uniform principles and guidelines around the sourcing of animal
L24@P1: derived raw materials
L25@P1: • To also ensure that appropriate due diligence is undertaken with regards to the
L26@P1: sourcing of products in relation to animal welfare
L27@P1: M&S MANDATORY PRINCIPLES FOR SOURCING
L28@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to protecting any endangered or vulnerable species and
L29@P1: to the prevention of cruelty. Through our supply chains we seek to promote, encourage and
L30@P1: foster higher animal welfare standards using codes, recommendations and audited supply
L31@P1: chains. We will continuously review our supply chains and where there are practices that
L32@P1: are of concern, we will take a considered course of action.
L33@P1: No animal will be slaughtered specifically for the manufacture or sourcing of M&S products.
L34@P1: PROHIBITED SOURCES
L35@P1: The following materials do not comply with our business principles for animal welfare and
L36@P1: therefore must not be used in any of our non-food products:
L37@P1: • Any material from any endangered species, defined as those which appear on the
L38@P1-2: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) (see www.cites.org/ Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L39@P2: Version Number 2.0 Page 3 of 5
L40@P2: Public Copy
L41@P2: for list of species) or the IUCN red list as Critically Endangered,
L42@P2: Endangered or Vulnerable (www.redlist.org/).
L43@P2: • No animal must be slaughtered specifically to produce any non- food M&S products.
L44@P2: • Fur: this includes farmed fur (e.g. fox, sable, mink, chinchilla, rabbit)
L45@P2: • Angora Rabbit fibre
L46@P2: • Alpaca fibre
L47@P2: • Astrakhan (Karakul) or any other leather/skin products which are the product of
L48@P2: unnatural abortions
L49@P2: • Any material obtained from live skinning (e.g. reptiles) or live boiling
L50@P2: • Any cow hides sourced from India
L51@P2: • Any animal derived bone or horn
L52@P2: • Any down or feathers from exotic birds, including but not limited to ostrich
L53@P2: • Any coral
L54@P2: RESTRICTED SOURCES
L55@P2: The following materials are currently accepted provided minimum requirements are met:
L56@P2: • Leather must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible Leather Sourcing Policy
L57@P2: • Animal Fibres (e.g. wool, cashmere) must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible
L58@P2: Wool Sourcing Policy and our Cashmere Code of Practice for animal welfare respectively.
L59@P2: All wool must be sourced from sheep that have not been mulesed
L60@P2: • Mohair must only be sourced through routes fully certified to the Textile Exchange
L61@P2: Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS)
L62@P2: • Feather and Down must not be obtained from the live plucking of birds or from birds used
L63@P2: in the production of Foie Gras. All Feather and Down must be sourced in compliance to
L64@P2: our Responsible Feather and Down Sourcing Policy
L65@P2: • All other animal derived materials must be sourced in accordance with this policy and
L66@P2: relevant details must be provided on an Animal derived material declaration form
L67@P2: • Any shell from vulnerable or endangered species must not be used (as defined by
L68@P2: CITES/IUCN red list)
L69@P2-3: • Only pearls form cultivated sources are allowed Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L70@P3: Version Number 2.0 Page 4 of 5
L71@P3: Public Copy
L72@P3: THE FIVE FREEDOMS OF ANIMAL WELFARE
L73@P3: In developing minimum standards for sourcing any animal product Marks & Spencer
L74@P3: consider the internationally recognised “Five Freedoms” as a framework and for guidance. It
L75@P3: is important that the sourcing of any animal derived materials for M&S are underpinned by
L76@P3: these principles:
L77@P3: 1. Freedom from Hunger and Thirst – by ready access to fresh water and a diet to
L78@P3: maintain full health and vigour
L79@P3: 2. Freedom from Discomfort – by providing an appropriate environment including
L80@P3: shelter and a comfortable resting area
L81@P3: 3. Freedom from Pain, Injury and Disease – by prevention or rapid diagnosis and
L82@P3: treatment
L83@P3: 4. Freedom to Express Normal Behaviour – by providing sufficient space, proper
L84@P3: facilities and company of the animal’s own kind
L85@P3: 5. Freedom from Fear and Distress – by ensuring conditions and treatment which
L86@P3: avoid mental suffering
L87@P3: ANIMAL TESTING
L88@P3: Marks and Spencer will not conduct or commission any tests on animals. All M&S own brand
L89@P3: cosmetic and household products and ingredients must be approved by the BUAV under
L90@P3: the Humane Cosmetics Standard, The Leaping Bunny Standard. This standard has been in
L91@P3: place since January 2006
L92@P3: PET ACCESSORIES
L93@P3: Any pet accessories are subject to all mandatory principles for sourcing. In addition, the
L94@P3: product itself must not compromise the welfare of the animal for which it is intended to be
L95@P3: used, using the Five Freedoms as a reference.
L96@P3: PRODUCT PROMOTION
L97@P3: Marks and Spencer will review all animal imagery used in the promotion of its products to
L98@P3: ensure that it does not endorse animal exploitation, cruelty or irresponsible use or
L99@P3: ownership.
L100@P3: DEFINITIONS
L101@P3: Animals: The Vegan Society understands the word animal to refer to the entire animal
L102@P3-4: kingdom, that is all vertebrates and multi-cellular invertebrates. The word may be used either Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L103@P4: Version Number 2.0 Page 5 of 5
L104@P4: Public Copy
L105@P4: as a noun or an adjective and to refer to a species, or an individual animal,
L106@P4: depending on context.
L107@P4: Animal derived materials: Materials including ingredients that have an animal (see above
L108@P4: definition), origin, regardless of whether they have been harvested form live or dead
L109@P4: animals.

L4@P0-1: ANIMAL WELFARE POLICYLatest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L5@P1: Version Number 2.0 Page 2 of 5
L6@P1: Public Copy
L7@P1: BACKGROUND
L8@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to using responsibly sourced raw materials including the
L9@P1: use of products derived from animals. This policy forms part of our commitment to uphold
L10@P1: the M&S animal welfare principles for all animal derived products we source.
L11@P1: SCOPE
L12@P1: This policy covers products sold in all Clothing, Home and Beauty areas that contain any
L13@P1: animal derived raw materials. The scope includes all main fabrics/textiles, trims,
L14@P1: componentry packaging, chemicals, pigments and dyestuffs.
L15@P1: This policy is intended to complement the additional specific sourcing policies for
L16@P1: Cashmere, Wool, Leather and Feather and Down.
L17@P1: RATONALE AND OBJECTIVES
L18@P1: • To ensure Marks & Spencer meets its long-standing commitment to improve animal
L19@P1: welfare in its supply chains and ensure all animal derived materials are sourced from
L20@P1: farms with good animal welfare practices. Marks & Spencer are committed to
L21@P1: improving animal welfare across our global supply chains and we are working to
L22@P1: source all animal-derived materials from farms with good animal welfare practices
L23@P1: • To lay out a set of uniform principles and guidelines around the sourcing of animal
L24@P1: derived raw materials
L25@P1: • To also ensure that appropriate due diligence is undertaken with regards to the
L26@P1: sourcing of products in relation to animal welfare
L27@P1: M&S MANDATORY PRINCIPLES FOR SOURCING
L28@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to protecting any endangered or vulnerable species and
L29@P1: to the prevention of cruelty. Through our supply chains we seek to promote, encourage and
L30@P1: foster higher animal welfare standards using codes, recommendations and audited supply
L31@P1: chains. We will continuously review our supply chains and where there are practices that
L32@P1: are of concern, we will take a considered course of action.
L33@P1: No animal will be slaughtered specifically for the manufacture or sourcing of M&S products.
L34@P1: PROHIBITED SOURCES
L35@P1: The following materials do not comply with our business principles for animal welfare and
L36@P1: therefore must not be used in any of our non-food products:
L37@P1: • Any material from any endangered species, defined as those which appear on the
L38@P1-2: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) (see www.cites.org/ Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L39@P2: Version Number 2.0 Page 3 of 5
L40@P2: Public Copy
L41@P2: for list of species) or the IUCN red list as Critically Endangered,
L42@P2: Endangered or Vulnerable (www.redlist.org/).
L43@P2: • No animal must be slaughtered specifically to produce any non- food M&S products.
L44@P2: • Fur: this includes farmed fur (e.g. fox, sable, mink, chinchilla, rabbit)
L45@P2: • Angora Rabbit fibre
L46@P2: • Alpaca fibre
L47@P2: • Astrakhan (Karakul) or any other leather/skin products which are the product of
L48@P2: unnatural abortions
L49@P2: • Any material obtained from live skinning (e.g. reptiles) or live boiling
L50@P2: • Any cow hides sourced from India
L51@P2: • Any animal derived bone or horn
L52@P2: • Any down or feathers from exotic birds, including but not limited to ostrich
L53@P2: • Any coral
L54@P2: RESTRICTED SOURCES
L55@P2: The following materials are currently accepted provided minimum requirements are met:
L56@P2: • Leather must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible Leather Sourcing Policy
L57@P2: • Animal Fibres (e.g. wool, cashmere) must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible
L58@P2: Wool Sourcing Policy and our Cashmere Code of Practice for animal welfare respectively.
L59@P2: All wool must be sourced from sheep that have not been mulesed
L60@P2: • Mohair must only be sourced through routes fully certified to the Textile Exchange
L61@P2: Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS)
L62@P2: • Feather and Down must not be obtained from the live plucking of birds or from birds used
L63@P2: in the production of Foie Gras. All Feather and Down must be sourced in compliance to
L64@P2: our Responsible Feather and Down Sourcing Policy
L65@P2: • All other animal derived materials must be sourced in accordance with this policy and
L66@P2: relevant details must be provided on an Animal derived material declaration form
L67@P2: • Any shell from vulnerable or endangered species must not be used (as defined by
L68@P2: CITES/IUCN red list)
L69@P2-3: • Only pearls form cultivated sources are allowed Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L70@P3: Version Number 2.0 Page 4 of 5
L71@P3: Public Copy
L72@P3: THE FIVE FREEDOMS OF ANIMAL WELFARE
L73@P3: In developing minimum standards for sourcing any animal product Marks & Spencer
L74@P3: consider the internationally recognised “Five Freedoms” as a framework and for guidance. It
L75@P3: is important that the sourcing of any animal derived materials for M&S are underpinned by
L76@P3: these principles:
L77@P3: 1. Freedom from Hunger and Thirst – by ready access to fresh water and a diet to
L78@P3: maintain full health and vigour
L79@P3: 2. Freedom from Discomfort – by providing an appropriate environment including
L80@P3: shelter and a comfortable resting area
L81@P3: 3. Freedom from Pain, Injury and Disease – by prevention or rapid diagnosis and
L82@P3: treatment
L83@P3: 4. Freedom to Express Normal Behaviour – by providing sufficient space, proper
L84@P3: facilities and company of the animal’s own kind
L85@P3: 5. Freedom from Fear and Distress – by ensuring conditions and treatment which
L86@P3: avoid mental suffering
L87@P3: ANIMAL TESTING
L88@P3: Marks and Spencer will not conduct or commission any tests on animals. All M&S own brand
L89@P3: cosmetic and household products and ingredients must be approved by the BUAV under
L90@P3: the Humane Cosmetics Standard, The Leaping Bunny Standard. This standard has been in
L91@P3: place since January 2006
L92@P3: PET ACCESSORIES
L93@P3: Any pet accessories are subject to all mandatory principles for sourcing. In addition, the
L94@P3: product itself must not compromise the welfare of the animal for which it is intended to be
L95@P3: used, using the Five Freedoms as a reference.
L96@P3: PRODUCT PROMOTION
L97@P3: Marks and Spencer will review all animal imagery used in the promotion of its products to
L98@P3: ensure that it does not endorse animal exploitation, cruelty or irresponsible use or
L99@P3: ownership.
L100@P3: DEFINITIONS
L101@P3: Animals: The Vegan Society understands the word animal to refer to the entire animal
L102@P3-4: kingdom, that is all vertebrates and multi-cellular invertebrates. The word may be used either Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L103@P4: Version Number 2.0 Page 5 of 5
L104@P4: Public Copy
L105@P4: as a noun or an adjective and to refer to a species, or an individual animal,
L106@P4: depending on context.
L107@P4: Animal derived materials: Materials including ingredients that have an animal (see above
L108@P4: definition), origin, regardless of whether they have been harvested form live or dead
L109@P4: animals.

L4@P0-1: ANIMAL WELFARE POLICYLatest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L5@P1: Version Number 2.0 Page 2 of 5
L6@P1: Public Copy
L7@P1: BACKGROUND
L8@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to using responsibly sourced raw materials including the
L9@P1: use of products derived from animals. This policy forms part of our commitment to uphold
L10@P1: the M&S animal welfare principles for all animal derived products we source.
L11@P1: SCOPE
L12@P1: This policy covers products sold in all Clothing, Home and Beauty areas that contain any
L13@P1: animal derived raw materials. The scope includes all main fabrics/textiles, trims,
L14@P1: componentry packaging, chemicals, pigments and dyestuffs.
L15@P1: This policy is intended to complement the additional specific sourcing policies for
L16@P1: Cashmere, Wool, Leather and Feather and Down.
L17@P1: RATONALE AND OBJECTIVES
L18@P1: • To ensure Marks & Spencer meets its long-standing commitment to improve animal
L19@P1: welfare in its supply chains and ensure all animal derived materials are sourced from
L20@P1: farms with good animal welfare practices. Marks & Spencer are committed to
L21@P1: improving animal welfare across our global supply chains and we are working to
L22@P1: source all animal-derived materials from farms with good animal welfare practices
L23@P1: • To lay out a set of uniform principles and guidelines around the sourcing of animal
L24@P1: derived raw materials
L25@P1: • To also ensure that appropriate due diligence is undertaken with regards to the
L26@P1: sourcing of products in relation to animal welfare
L27@P1: M&S MANDATORY PRINCIPLES FOR SOURCING
L28@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to protecting any endangered or vulnerable species and
L29@P1: to the prevention of cruelty. Through our supply chains we seek to promote, encourage and
L30@P1: foster higher animal welfare standards using codes, recommendations and audited supply
L31@P1: chains. We will continuously review our supply chains and where there are practices that
L32@P1: are of concern, we will take a considered course of action.
L33@P1: No animal will be slaughtered specifically for the manufacture or sourcing of M&S products.
L34@P1: PROHIBITED SOURCES
L35@P1: The following materials do not comply with our business principles for animal welfare and
L36@P1: therefore must not be used in any of our non-food products:
L37@P1: • Any material from any endangered species, defined as those which appear on the
L38@P1-2: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) (see www.cites.org/ Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy

L41@P2: for list of species) or the IUCN red list as Critically Endangered,

L43@P2: • No animal must be slaughtered specifically to produce any non- food M&S products.
L44@P2: • Fur: this includes farmed fur (e.g. fox, sable, mink, chinchilla, rabbit)

L46@P2: • Alpaca fibre

L73@P3: In developing minimum standards for sourcing any animal product Marks & Spencer
L74@P3: consider the internationally recognised “Five Freedoms” as a framework and for guidance. It
L75@P3: is important that the sourcing of any animal derived materials for M&S are underpinned by

L7@P1: BACKGROUND
L8@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to using responsibly sourced raw materials including the
L9@P1: use of products derived from animals. This policy forms part of our commitment to uphold
L10@P1: the M&S animal welfare principles for all animal derived products we source.

L12@P1: This policy covers products sold in all Clothing, Home and Beauty areas that contain any
L13@P1: animal derived raw materials. The scope includes all main fabrics/textiles, trims,
L14@P1: componentry packaging, chemicals, pigments and dyestuffs.
L15@P1: This policy is intended to complement the additional specific sourcing policies for
L16@P1: Cashmere, Wool, Leather and Feather and Down.
L17@P1: RATONALE AND OBJECTIVES
L18@P1: • To ensure Marks & Spencer meets its long-standing commitment to improve animal
L19@P1: welfare in its supply chains and ensure all animal derived materials are sourced from
L20@P1: farms with good animal welfare practices. Marks & Spencer are committed to
L21@P1: improving animal welfare across our global supply chains and we are working to
L22@P1: source all animal-derived materials from farms with good animal welfare practices
L23@P1: • To lay out a set of uniform principles and guidelines around the sourcing of animal
L24@P1: derived raw materials
L25@P1: • To also ensure that appropriate due diligence is undertaken with regards to the
L26@P1: sourcing of products in relation to animal welfare
L27@P1: M&S MANDATORY PRINCIPLES FOR SOURCING
L28@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to protecting any endangered or vulnerable species and
L29@P1: to the prevention of cruelty. Through our supply chains we seek to promote, encourage and
L30@P1: foster higher animal welfare standards using codes, recommendations and audited supply
L31@P1: chains. We will continuously review our supply chains and where there are practices that
L32@P1: are of concern, we will take a considered course of action.
L33@P1: No animal will be slaughtered specifically for the manufacture or sourcing of M&S products.
L34@P1: PROHIBITED SOURCES
L35@P1: The following materials do not comply with our business principles for animal welfare and
L36@P1: therefore must not be used in any of our non-food products:
L37@P1: • Any material from any endangered species, defined as those which appear on the
L38@P1-2: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) (see www.cites.org/ Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L39@P2: Version Number 2.0 Page 3 of 5
L40@P2: Public Copy
L41@P2: for list of species) or the IUCN red list as Critically Endangered,
L42@P2: Endangered or Vulnerable (www.redlist.org/).
L43@P2: • No animal must be slaughtered specifically to produce any non- food M&S products.
L44@P2: • Fur: this includes farmed fur (e.g. fox, sable, mink, chinchilla, rabbit)
L45@P2: • Angora Rabbit fibre
L46@P2: • Alpaca fibre
L47@P2: • Astrakhan (Karakul) or any other leather/skin products which are the product of
L48@P2: unnatural abortions
L49@P2: • Any material obtained from live skinning (e.g. reptiles) or live boiling
L50@P2: • Any cow hides sourced from India
L51@P2: • Any animal derived bone or horn
L52@P2: • Any down or feathers from exotic birds, including but not limited to ostrich
L53@P2: • Any coral
L54@P2: RESTRICTED SOURCES
L55@P2: The following materials are currently accepted provided minimum requirements are met:
L56@P2: • Leather must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible Leather Sourcing Policy
L57@P2: • Animal Fibres (e.g. wool, cashmere) must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible
L58@P2: Wool Sourcing Policy and our Cashmere Code of Practice for animal welfare respectively.
L59@P2: All wool must be sourced from sheep that have not been mulesed
L60@P2: • Mohair must only be sourced through routes fully certified to the Textile Exchange
L61@P2: Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS)
L62@P2: • Feather and Down must not be obtained from the live plucking of birds or from birds used
L63@P2: in the production of Foie Gras. All Feather and Down must be sourced in compliance to
L64@P2: our Responsible Feather and Down Sourcing Policy
L65@P2: • All other animal derived materials must be sourced in accordance with this policy and
L66@P2: relevant details must be provided on an Animal derived material declaration form
L67@P2: • Any shell from vulnerable or endangered species must not be used (as defined by
L68@P2: CITES/IUCN red list)
L69@P2-3: • Only pearls form cultivated sources are allowed Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L70@P3: Version Number 2.0 Page 4 of 5
L71@P3: Public Copy
L72@P3: THE FIVE FREEDOMS OF ANIMAL WELFARE
L73@P3: In developing minimum standards for sourcing any animal product Marks & Spencer
L74@P3: consider the internationally recognised “Five Freedoms” as a framework and for guidance. It
L75@P3: is important that the sourcing of any animal derived materials for M&S are underpinned by
L76@P3: these principles:
L77@P3: 1. Freedom from Hunger and Thirst – by ready access to fresh water and a diet to
L78@P3: maintain full health and vigour
L79@P3: 2. Freedom from Discomfort – by providing an appropriate environment including
L80@P3: shelter and a comfortable resting area
L81@P3: 3. Freedom from Pain, Injury and Disease – by prevention or rapid diagnosis and
L82@P3: treatment
L83@P3: 4. Freedom to Express Normal Behaviour – by providing sufficient space, proper
L84@P3: facilities and company of the animal’s own kind
L85@P3: 5. Freedom from Fear and Distress – by ensuring conditions and treatment which
L86@P3: avoid mental suffering
L87@P3: ANIMAL TESTING
L88@P3: Marks and Spencer will not conduct or commission any tests on animals. All M&S own brand
L89@P3: cosmetic and household products and ingredients must be approved by the BUAV under
L90@P3: the Humane Cosmetics Standard, The Leaping Bunny Standard. This standard has been in
L91@P3: place since January 2006
L92@P3: PET ACCESSORIES
L93@P3: Any pet accessories are subject to all mandatory principles for sourcing. In addition, the
L94@P3: product itself must not compromise the welfare of the animal for which it is intended to be
L95@P3: used, using the Five Freedoms as a reference.
L96@P3: PRODUCT PROMOTION
L97@P3: Marks and Spencer will review all animal imagery used in the promotion of its products to
L98@P3: ensure that it does not endorse animal exploitation, cruelty or irresponsible use or
L99@P3: ownership.
L100@P3: DEFINITIONS
L101@P3: Animals: The Vegan Society understands the word animal to refer to the entire animal
L102@P3-4: kingdom, that is all vertebrates and multi-cellular invertebrates. The word may be used either Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy

###

What range of AVEENO ® should I be using?

Image: flat-lat-2 
The AVEENO^{®} Daily Moisturising Range (green) is formulated to nourish and protect normal to dry skin.
The AVEENO^{®} Skin Relief Range (dark blue) will moisturise and cleanse to help heal dry, irritable skin
The AVEENO^{®} Dermexa Range (light blue) is for very dry itchy skin, and is also suitable for people who may be prone to eczema
###

What are some good tips for dry skincare?

Image: skin microbiome diagram 1 
Your skin draws moisture from the environment, your diet and your skincare routine. The water content of the outermost layer of your skin (the epidermis) also tends to reflect the level of humidity around it, so following the same skincare routine year-round may not be working when the humidity drops.

Here are a few simple ways to keep your skin hydrated and combat dry, itchy skin:
  * Limit time in the shower or bath, we recommend 5-10 minutes.

  * Moisturise immediately after washing. This gives the highest chance of trapping existing moisture in your skin.

  * Using a humidifier will help add much-needed moisture to the air.

  * Choosing fabrics such as cotton and silk, that will allow your skin to breathe.

  * Make sure to include lots of healthy fats like fish, walnuts, olive oil and avocados in your diet, as well as drinking lots of water.
###

What are the skincare benefits of oat?

Image: aveen woman back 1 
Aveeno harnesses the power of the oat through many ways:

Oat Extract/Oat Essence (liquid produced from the oat plant) is naturally rich in Avenanthramides, which are known for their soothing and potent antioxidant properties.

Colloidal Oatmeal (a powder produced by the fine grinding of oats) has moisturising properties that help prevent water loss from the skin.
Oat Oil (a liquid extracted from oat grain) is naturally rich in lips which are essential components for a proper functioning skin barrier.
###

Is AVEENO ® suitable for eczema-prone skin?

Our Dermexa Range is formulated for very dry itchy skin, and is also suitable for eczema- prone skin.

What are prebiotics and probiotics?

Although they sound pretty similar, probiotics and prebiotics are two vastly different things with specific functions. Probiotics are living microorganisms that are found both naturally in your body and in food and supplements. When consumed or applied to the skin, they provide a wealth of positive benefits for the body, including:

  * Promoting good gut health

  * Strengthening skin overall
Prebiotics on the other hand aren’t actually alive. They are non-digestible ingredients that help to nourish the good bacteria in your gut or on your skin and balance the microbiome.

When probiotics and prebiotics are combined, whether that be in skin cream or in foods, they join forces to become what’s known as a synbiotic. Common synbiotics include supplements, additives and certain foods like yoghurt and cheese.
###

What is the skin microbiome?

Your skin’s microbiome is the collective name for the ecosystem of tiny microorganisms that live on and beneath the surface of your skin. It’s made up of a diverse range of different organisms playing different roles, including:

  * Bacteria – A variety of microscopic organisms which can be both potentially harmful and beneficial to the health of your skin

  * Fungi – Microbes that can be harmful or helpful, a heavy build-up can cause fungal infections
  * Mites – Insect-like microorganisms, invisible to the human eye, that can cause irritation in large numbers

  * Viruses – Microscopic molecules that, if allowed to multiply, can cause infection or illness on the skin
###

Is Aveeno gluten free?

We are unable to recommend AVEENO^{®} products for coeliacs since we cannot confirm the complete absence of gluten in our oat ingredients.

###

What is Aveeno Skin Renewal?

The Aveeno^{®} Skin Renewal Body Range has been formulated to address rough & bumpy skin, uneven tone and loss of firmness concerns. Even more importantly, the products are formulated for sensitive skin.
The range comprising of a Gentle Scrub , Smoothing Cream and Firming Lotion is formulated with nourishing oat known to help support the microbiome and naturally derived PHA: a combination of ingredients selected specifically with sensitive skin in mind. The naturally derived PHA was selected due to its larger molecule size, which doesn’t penetrate the skin as deeply & is therefore more suitable for sensitive skin than other skincare acid groups (AHA’s, BHA’s).
###

Who is Aveeno Skin Renewal for?

The Aveeno Skin Renewal range is formulated for those with dry, sensitive skin. There are three products in the range with different benefits:

  * •Gentle Body Scrub: A precursor to either the Smoothing Cream or Firming Lotion. Formulated with prebiotic oat + niacinamide + naturally derived PHA to get rid of dead skin build-up. Helping to boost skin's natural renewal process through gentle exfoliation. Ensuring skin is ready for smoothing or firming.
  * •Smoothing Cream: Formulated with prebiotic oat + niacinamide + naturally derived PHA to leave dry, rough & bumpy skin feeling smoothed, soft and moisturised in just one night. Also suitable for people with Keratosis Pilaris
  * •Firming Lotion: clinically-proven to moisturise and improve skin elasticity in dry, unfirm and uneven skin. As well as nourishing oat and naturally derived PHA, it contains blackberry leaf extract, known to help enhance collagen and elastin recovery, and can help protect against premature ageing.
###

What is PHA? Are PHA’s good for the skin

Polyhydroxy acids (PHAs) are a popular skincare ingredient that have a wide range of benefits including moisturisation, renewal, and  can enhace stratum corneum barrier function . PHAs can also be better for sensitive skin than other commonly used chemical exfoliants, such as AHAS and BHAs, as they have a larger molecular structure so don’t penetrate as deeply into the skin.

For more information on PHAs see here ###

What other key ingredients are in skin renewal

All three products in the range contain both Nourishing Oat & Naturally Derived PHA to help support the skins microbiome and promote skin renewal for improved tone & texture.

Both the Gentle Body Scrub & Smoothing Cream also contain niacinamide which is known to help brighten skin & reduce discoloration. Whilst the Gentle Body Scrub also contains naturally derived beads, and helps promote skin cell turnover.
The Firming Lotion contains Blackberry Leaf Extract known to help enhance collagen & elastin recovery.
###

Is Skin Renewal suitable for sensitive skin?

Skin Renewal is formulated for sensitive skin. Featuring both nourishing oat & naturally derived PHA. Ingredients known to be gentler on sensitive skin types. Read more about PHA here .

###

Is Skin Renewal dermatologist tested?

All three products in the Skin Renewal range are dermatologist tested.
###

How often should I use skin renewal?

The Gentle Body Scrub can be used 1-2 times per week and can be incorporated into usual shower or bath regime. The Smoothing Cream or Firming Lotion can be used daily to help smooth, moisturise or firm skin.
###

How to apply skin renewal?

 Gentle Body Scrub

Apply a generous amount onto dry or damp skin and massage in circular motions, paying particular attention to dry and rough areas such as elbows, knees and heels. Rinse off with water. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.

 Smoothing Cream

Apply liberally all over body to leave your skin feeling smooth & moisturised. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.

 Firming Lotion
Use daily to moisturise & visibly firm. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.
###

Is Skin Renewal fragrance free?

All three Skin Renewal products are fragrance free.

Sustainability Statement
Our Sustainability Statement
Innovation, functionality and reliability are at the heart of every product we sell and we strive to ensure every range we offer reflects these values.
We also have a responsibility to understand the implications of our actions across our entire business and have an unwavering desire to ensure fairness in everything we do.
Our aim is focussed on three factors: our People, our Products and our Impact.
Our People
At Stellar we understand that we are all different and we value and respect these differences, not just in relation to gender, ethnicity, ability, age, sexual orientation and faith, but also in terms of background, education, family and care responsibilities.
We see these differences as key contributors to helping us achieve better results and to better serve our customers and consumers. We are also convinced that creating an inclusive environment, where everyone feels valued and able to bring their differences to work creates a more stimulating and rewarding atmosphere for everyone to work in.
At Stellar we ensure, through internal measurement and audit that we comply with all applicable employment laws and commit to ensuring fairness in the recruitment and development of all colleagues. We are transparent during our recruitment processes and provide clarity and feedback to all third parties with whom we partner.
Our company handbook, highlights our code of conduct and expectations which reflect the levels of decency and respect we expect all of the Stellar team to achieve.
At Stellar, we believe we have a responsibility to conduct every aspect of our business in an ethical way. We expect the same from our suppliers and we focus on helping them to ensure safe working conditions and environmental responsibility.
We also believe that all businesses must play their part in tackling slavery, in line with the Modern Slavery Act of 2015, Stellar will commit to annually reviewing our policies to ensure compliance.
Our Products
We strive to ensure that every product we source and all of our manufacturing partners achieve the highest safety, ethical and environmental standards. To ensure this we undertake regular supplier visits, and comply to the relevant standards.
We seek to hold every safety and compliance certificate legally required.
Our Impact
We are devoted to reducing the impact that our business practices have on our environment and we have identified 3 areas that we believe will help us achieve this:
1 – Reduction of single use plastic
Our ambition is to remove single use plastic from our business by 2025. This will be achieved by working closely with our manufacturing partners. We will work with our customers to ensure we are able to meet their product requirements whilst achieving our own company objectives through creative, collaborative solutions and effective packaging management.
Our journey toward this ambition has already begun with the removal; of all polybags from our cutlery sets and blister carded packaging. Also with our direct consumer delivery process consisting of 100% recyclable paper protection instead of plastic or polystyrene.
2 – Improved working environment
Our commitment is also focussed on educating our own team as to the impact they have on their environment. All of the Stellar team have been provided with re-usable hydration bottles and are encouraged to use our in house recycling stations for all waste management
We have upgraded our warehouse lighting systems to be run from a sensored LED platform. This has contributed to a drop of 40% in electricity usage.
All new company cars issued by the company will have a maximum carbon emission set. Which we will seek to reduce this over time.
3 – Packaging
Working closely with our packaging partners, manufacturers and logistics providers we are looking to source ethically produced and fully recyclable packaging solutions for all of our products. We will also actively reduce the packaging utilised throughout our supply chain, including deliveries, whilst maintaining product integrity commit to develop materials that have zero impact on our environment.
We invite suggestions from consumers and customers to help drive our ongoing company developments, so get in touch.
Clearly, our expectations are high but we feel they need to be to ensure we can create a more inclusive and sustainable environment.

Sustainability Statement
Our Sustainability Statement
Innovation, functionality and reliability are at the heart of every product we sell and we strive to ensure every range we offer reflects these values.
We also have a responsibility to understand the implications of our actions across our entire business and have an unwavering desire to ensure fairness in everything we do.
Our aim is focussed on three factors: our People, our Products and our Impact.
Our People
At Stellar we understand that we are all different and we value and respect these differences, not just in relation to gender, ethnicity, ability, age, sexual orientation and faith, but also in terms of background, education, family and care responsibilities.
We see these differences as key contributors to helping us achieve better results and to better serve our customers and consumers. We are also convinced that creating an inclusive environment, where everyone feels valued and able to bring their differences to work creates a more stimulating and rewarding atmosphere for everyone to work in.
At Stellar we ensure, through internal measurement and audit that we comply with all applicable employment laws and commit to ensuring fairness in the recruitment and development of all colleagues. We are transparent during our recruitment processes and provide clarity and feedback to all third parties with whom we partner.
Our company handbook, highlights our code of conduct and expectations which reflect the levels of decency and respect we expect all of the Stellar team to achieve.
At Stellar, we believe we have a responsibility to conduct every aspect of our business in an ethical way. We expect the same from our suppliers and we focus on helping them to ensure safe working conditions and environmental responsibility.
We also believe that all businesses must play their part in tackling slavery, in line with the Modern Slavery Act of 2015, Stellar will commit to annually reviewing our policies to ensure compliance.
Our Products
We strive to ensure that every product we source and all of our manufacturing partners achieve the highest safety, ethical and environmental standards. To ensure this we undertake regular supplier visits, and comply to the relevant standards.
We seek to hold every safety and compliance certificate legally required.
Our Impact
We are devoted to reducing the impact that our business practices have on our environment and we have identified 3 areas that we believe will help us achieve this:
1 – Reduction of single use plastic
Our ambition is to remove single use plastic from our business by 2025. This will be achieved by working closely with our manufacturing partners. We will work with our customers to ensure we are able to meet their product requirements whilst achieving our own company objectives through creative, collaborative solutions and effective packaging management.
Our journey toward this ambition has already begun with the removal; of all polybags from our cutlery sets and blister carded packaging. Also with our direct consumer delivery process consisting of 100% recyclable paper protection instead of plastic or polystyrene.
2 – Improved working environment
Our commitment is also focussed on educating our own team as to the impact they have on their environment. All of the Stellar team have been provided with re-usable hydration bottles and are encouraged to use our in house recycling stations for all waste management
We have upgraded our warehouse lighting systems to be run from a sensored LED platform. This has contributed to a drop of 40% in electricity usage.
All new company cars issued by the company will have a maximum carbon emission set. Which we will seek to reduce this over time.
3 – Packaging
Working closely with our packaging partners, manufacturers and logistics providers we are looking to source ethically produced and fully recyclable packaging solutions for all of our products. We will also actively reduce the packaging utilised throughout our supply chain, including deliveries, whilst maintaining product integrity commit to develop materials that have zero impact on our environment.
We invite suggestions from consumers and customers to help drive our ongoing company developments, so get in touch.
Clearly, our expectations are high but we feel they need to be to ensure we can create a more inclusive and sustainable environment.

Sustainability Statement
Our Sustainability Statement
Innovation, functionality and reliability are at the heart of every product we sell and we strive to ensure every range we offer reflects these values.
We also have a responsibility to understand the implications of our actions across our entire business and have an unwavering desire to ensure fairness in everything we do.
Our aim is focussed on three factors: our People, our Products and our Impact.
Our People
At Stellar we understand that we are all different and we value and respect these differences, not just in relation to gender, ethnicity, ability, age, sexual orientation and faith, but also in terms of background, education, family and care responsibilities.
We see these differences as key contributors to helping us achieve better results and to better serve our customers and consumers. We are also convinced that creating an inclusive environment, where everyone feels valued and able to bring their differences to work creates a more stimulating and rewarding atmosphere for everyone to work in.
At Stellar we ensure, through internal measurement and audit that we comply with all applicable employment laws and commit to ensuring fairness in the recruitment and development of all colleagues. We are transparent during our recruitment processes and provide clarity and feedback to all third parties with whom we partner.
Our company handbook, highlights our code of conduct and expectations which reflect the levels of decency and respect we expect all of the Stellar team to achieve.
At Stellar, we believe we have a responsibility to conduct every aspect of our business in an ethical way. We expect the same from our suppliers and we focus on helping them to ensure safe working conditions and environmental responsibility.
We also believe that all businesses must play their part in tackling slavery, in line with the Modern Slavery Act of 2015, Stellar will commit to annually reviewing our policies to ensure compliance.
Our Products
We strive to ensure that every product we source and all of our manufacturing partners achieve the highest safety, ethical and environmental standards. To ensure this we undertake regular supplier visits, and comply to the relevant standards.
We seek to hold every safety and compliance certificate legally required.
Our Impact
We are devoted to reducing the impact that our business practices have on our environment and we have identified 3 areas that we believe will help us achieve this:
1 – Reduction of single use plastic
Our ambition is to remove single use plastic from our business by 2025. This will be achieved by working closely with our manufacturing partners. We will work with our customers to ensure we are able to meet their product requirements whilst achieving our own company objectives through creative, collaborative solutions and effective packaging management.
Our journey toward this ambition has already begun with the removal; of all polybags from our cutlery sets and blister carded packaging. Also with our direct consumer delivery process consisting of 100% recyclable paper protection instead of plastic or polystyrene.
2 – Improved working environment
Our commitment is also focussed on educating our own team as to the impact they have on their environment. All of the Stellar team have been provided with re-usable hydration bottles and are encouraged to use our in house recycling stations for all waste management
We have upgraded our warehouse lighting systems to be run from a sensored LED platform. This has contributed to a drop of 40% in electricity usage.
All new company cars issued by the company will have a maximum carbon emission set. Which we will seek to reduce this over time.
3 – Packaging
Working closely with our packaging partners, manufacturers and logistics providers we are looking to source ethically produced and fully recyclable packaging solutions for all of our products. We will also actively reduce the packaging utilised throughout our supply chain, including deliveries, whilst maintaining product integrity commit to develop materials that have zero impact on our environment.
We invite suggestions from consumers and customers to help drive our ongoing company developments, so get in touch.
Clearly, our expectations are high but we feel they need to be to ensure we can create a more inclusive and sustainable environment.

product.detailed_description: Fragrance Light the wick and this hand-poured offering will transport you to an indulgent, tropical palace, where the exotic aroma of black orchid blends with notes of rich amber and spiced musk, pamperingly enriched with a smooth touch of vanilla. About the Brand Pintail Candles is a family business that has been hand-making candles in the Lake District for over 30 years, using the traditional double-pour method. The company is dedicated to creating its candles in an ethical and environmentally friendly way: the wax it uses is a recycled by-product of other industries, its workshop is powered by renewable energy, its components come from fellow UK manufacturers and it pays a living wage to its staff, protecting local jobs in Britain and the communities they support. Burn time: Up to 35 hours.
product.other_information: Candle Diameter: 75mm Candle Height: 65mm Volume: 178ml Weight: 225g
product.preparation_and_usage: Place on a stable, level, heat resistant surface away fromdraughts and combustible materials. Not wood, plastic or any material that may mark with heat. Keep out of the reach of children and animals. Always trim wick to 5mm prior to each use. Stop when 5mm of wax remains. Keep wax pool clear of foreign objects e.g. matches, as this may cause a dangerous second source of flame. Never leave a burning candle unattended. Container may become hot during use. Extinguish if flame becomes enlarged or smokes. Do not burn this candle for more than 3 hours at any one time.

L59: We are a UK-based private label and white label candle manufacturer, producing high-quality candles for retailers, hospitality businesses and brands.
L60: 
L61: From our Lake District workshop, we offer white label candles, private label candle manufacturing, and scalable production with low minimums and full UK compliance.
L62: 
L63: cite22†Get in touch L64: 
L65:   * ### White Label Candle Manufacturing (UK)
L66: Our white label candle service is designed for brands who want speed, simplicity and proven bestsellers.
L67: 
L68: You choose from our existing range of candle vessels and fragrances. We manufacture, label and supply candles under your brand name — without the cost or lead times of developing products from scratch.
L69: 
L70: White label candles are ideal for:
L71: 
L72: Retailers launching home fragrance ranges
L73: Visitor attractions and gift shops
L74: Corporate gifting and subscription boxes
L75: Hospitality businesses
L76: 
L77: What’s included:
L78: UK-made, hand-poured candles
L79: Proven fragrance blends
L80: Stock vessels and formats
L81: Fast turnaround times
L82: Low minimum order quantities
L83: 
L84: If you’re searching for white label candles in the UK, this is the fastest way to market.
L85: 
L86:   * ### Private Label Candle Manufacturing (UK)
L87: 
L88: Our private label candle manufacturing service offers more flexibility, while keeping production efficient and commercially viable.
L89: We manufacture candles to your specifications using your branding, with guidance throughout the process to ensure the final product works both aesthetically and operationally.
L90: 
L91: Private label candle manufacturing includes:
L92: 
L93: Custom printed labels or supplied artwork
L94: Choice of candle formats and vessels
L95: Fragrance selection or refinement
L96: Retail-ready finishing and packaging
L97: CLP-compliant labelling and batch codes
L98: This service suits brands who want a distinctive product without the cost and complexity of overseas production.
L99: 
L100: If you’re looking for private label candles UK-made, we offer a practical, experienced manufacturing partner.
L101: 
L102: Get In Touch (info@pintailcandles.com)
L103: 
L104:   * cite23†Image L105: ### Brand Development
L106: 
L107: Want a bespoke in house brand but have no idea where to start? We’ve developed for supermarkets, high street retailers and the best of independents and we can help you too.
L108: 
L109:   * cite24†Image L110: 
L111: ### Packaging Design
L112: 
L113: We are famous for our ‘paint pot’ tins but your packaging is totally bespoke. From boxes made in Yorkshire to ceramics fired in Stoke and glass recycled in Kent, lets find the perfect containers together.
L114: 
L115:   * cite25†Image L116: ### Bespoke Fragrance Blends
L117: 
L118: The fragrance world is your oyster. Choose from off the shelf guaranteed best sellers to bespoke blends that exist only for you. We work across the best of natural and synthetic blends, and natural and paraffin waxes.
L119: 
L120:   * cite26†Image L121: 
L122: ### Manufacture
L123: 
L124: We make everything here in our Cumbrian workshop, from raw materials sourced in the UK. Handmade by our team of expert artisans. Our expert logistics team will ensure everything makes it to you on time.
L125: 
L126:   * cite27†Image L127: ### Iterate and Expand
L128: 
L129: Want to do more? Our textiles manufacturing is also onsite in Cumbria. From kitchen linens to elegant tablescapes and embroidered finishes - where else could we take your homeware brand?
L130: 
L131:   * cite28†Image: The team at Pintail Candles L132: 
L133: ### Get In Touch
L134: 
L135: Drop us a line, and lets start dreaming together.
L136: 
L137: Email us on info@pintailcandles.com or hit the contact form and we'll be in touch ASAP to kick everything off.
L138: ## Who We Manufacture Candles For
L139: 
L140: We manufacture candles for a wide range of UK and international clients, including:
L141: 
L142: Independent retailers
L143: National retail chains
L144: Hotels and hospitality groups
L145: Museums, gardens and heritage sites
L146: Corporate gifting companies
L147: Lifestyle and subscription brands
L148: 
L149: Whether you’re launching a first range or expanding an established one, our manufacturing model is designed to scale with you.
L150: ## Why Choose a UK Candle Manufacturer?
L151: 
L152: Choosing a UK-based candle manufacturer offers clear advantages:
L153: 
L154: Shorter lead times and reliable supply
L155: No import delays or customs costs
L156: Easier communication and quality control
L157: Full UK regulatory compliance
L158: Lower minimum order quantities
L159: Ethical, local manufacturing
L160: 
L161: All candles are produced in-house in our Lake District workshop, allowing us to maintain consistency, quality and flexibility.
L162: ## Private & White Label Candle Manufacturing FAQs
L163: 
L164: What are your minimum order quantities?
L165: Minimums vary by product type. Orders start from 96 units per product, in multiples of 48.
L166: 
L167: Can you hold labels and manufacture in stages?
L168: Yes. We can print and hold labels, allowing stock to be produced and released in phases.
L169: 
L170: Do you provide CLP-compliant labelling?
L171: Yes. All candles are supplied with compliant labelling, batch codes and required safety information.
L172: Are your candles made in the UK?
L173: Yes. All manufacturing takes place in our Lake District workshop.
L174: 
L175: Can I reorder without redesigning?
L176: Absolutely. Many of our partners work with us on repeat and seasonal production runs.

product.name: Price's Tropical Citrus Medium Jar Candle
product.ingredients: Contains: paraffin wax, linalool, (R)-p-Mentha-1,8-diene
product.allergens: May produce an allergic reaction.
product.detailed_description: Want to transform any room to a tropical Mediterranean getaway? Our Tropical Citrus candle will fill your room with the scent of fresh juicy oranges, zesty lemons and luscious limes, a smell everyone loves. Invigorate your early mornings or unwind after a long day with this scent and every day will feel like summer. Made with the highest quality waxes and fragrance bespoke to us, this candle is easy to use and relight, giving up to 150 hours of burn time.
product.preparation_and_usage: Never leave burning candles unattended. Always read and follow manufacturer’s instructions supplied with candles and candle holders. Burn out of reach of children and pets. Extinguish candles with a candle snuffer. Do not blow them out. Never use water to extinguish a candle. Ensure candles are placed at least 10cm / 4 inches apart and allow headroom above the candle for the heat to disperse. Ensure candles are burned away from flammable items. Candles should be burned away from other sources of heat such as television sets and away from direct sunlight. Candles should be burned in an area free from draughts. Trim wick to 1cm / ½ inch before lighting or relighting. If the candle smokes, extinguish and trim the wick. Ensure candles are burned in an upright position. Do not move candles when lit or the wax is still liquid.
product.manufacturer: SER, STRADA QUAGLIA, 26- 10026 SANTENA- ITALIA
product.return_to_address: Price's Patent Candles Ltd, 16 Hudson Rd, Elm Farm Industrial Estate, Bedford, MK41 0LZ

FAQ 

1. Frequently asked questions 

How do I track my parcel? 

As soon as your parcel has been shipped, you will receive an e-mail notification including a link enabling you to track its progress. 

Where do you ship your products? 

We deliver to mainland France and to the following countries: Belgium, Germany, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Estonia, Spain, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Portugal, Slovenia, Slovakia, Ireland, Italy, Denmark, Poland, Serbia, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Finland, Greece, Iceland, Malta, Norway, Romania, Guyane FR, Martinique, Réunion, St Pierre et Miquelon, Mayotte, Guadeloupe, Polynesia FR, New Caledonia, Wallis and Futuna. 

How long does it take for my order to be delivered? 

Your products will be delivered to the address indicated, within a maximum of 5 working days in metropolitan France and 9 working days for Europe. Except in special cases (package too heavy, or quantity of products too large) or unavailability of one or more products, the products ordered will be delivered at once. 

How can I contact you? 

You can contact the Petit Olivier teams via the chat at the bottom of the page, by e-mail at manon@lepetitolivier.fr, or via the contact form on our site or the "Need help" tab in the site footer. 

For all partnership requests or applications, please write to us at communication@phoceennedecosmetique.fr or contact us via our social networks Facebook or Instagram. 

I've tried to contact you, how soon can I expect a reply? 

If you would like a quick response, we recommend that you visit the "Need help" page on our website. If you have contacted us via e-mail or the contact form on our site, please allow 48 to 72 hours. Our customer service is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 5:30pm. 

2. Payment 

What payment methods do you offer? 

You can pay for your order via PayPal, Apple Pay, or by credit card, American Express, Visa and MasterCard. 

If, for any reason, you are unable to complete your order, please contact us by e-mail: manon@lepetitolivier.fr. We will be happy to help you. 

3. Delivery & Returns 

Where can your products be delivered? 

We deliver to mainland France and the following countries: Belgium, Germany, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Estonia, Spain, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Portugal, Slovenia, Slovakia, Ireland, Italy, Denmark, Poland, Serbia, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Finland, Greece, Iceland, Malta, Norway, Romania, Guyane FR, Martinique, Réunion, St Pierre et Miquelon, Mayotte, Guadeloupe, Polynesia FR, New Caledonia, Wallis and Futuna. 

What are the delivery times? 

Your products will be delivered to the address indicated, within a maximum of 5 working days in metropolitan France and 9 working days for Europe. Except in special cases (package too heavy, or quantity of products too large) or unavailability of one or more products, the products ordered will be delivered at once. 

How much does delivery cost? 

In France, home delivery costs €5.99 and is free for orders over €45. Delivery to a relay point or post office costs €4.99 and is free for orders over €40. For international orders, home delivery is offered at variable rates depending on the destination and weight of your parcel. 

Who delivers the parcels? 

For parcel delivery, we have selected our partner Colissimo - La Poste. 

Can I change the delivery address once the order has been validated? 

Once your delivery address has been transmitted via your order, it is definitive. 

Puis-je modifier ou annuler ma commande ? 

Il n'est pas possible de modifier le contenu de votre commande, ni son adresse de livraison, une fois que celle-ci a été validée. 

Cependant, l'annulation de votre commande est possible si sa préparation n'a pas encore démarré et qu'elle n'a pas quitté notre entrepôt. Il est donc impératif de nous contacter très rapidement (manon@lepetitolivier.fr), nous ferons tout notre possible pour vous aider. Si malheureusement l'annulation n'est plus possible, vous pourrez toujours nous la retourner après réception (via une demande de retour), ou refuser la livraison afin d'obtenir un remboursement. 

My parcel says delivered but I haven't received anything? 

Sometimes the parcel has been received by a janitor or neighbor, or the delivery status has been updated too early. However, if after checking, you still think your parcel has been mislaid, write to us at manon@lepetitolivier.fr . We'll get back to you as soon as possible to find a solution! 

My parcel has been returned to sender. What should I do? 

If the address you have provided is incomplete, if the parcel has been damaged in transit, or if we have been unable to deliver it to you, it may be returned to us. In this case, write to us at manon@lepetitolivier.fr, specifying your order number: our teams will get back to you as soon as possible! 

Can I return my order? 

If you are not satisfied with an item, you can return it within 14 days of receiving your parcel. For all returns, please contact us at manon@lepetitolivier.fr , mentioning your order number, the items you wish to return and the reason for your return. In accordance with the provisions of article L 221-28 5° of the French Consumer Code, refunds will only be made if products are returned in their original packaging and in perfect condition. Damaged, soiled or incomplete items cannot be returned. Return shipping costs will be borne exclusively by the purchaser. 

What should I do if my order is damaged? 

Unfortunately, some products may be damaged in transit. If this is the case, please send a message to our customer service department with photos to the following e-mail address: manon@lepetitolivier.fr . We will get back to you as soon as possible. 

What should I do if my order is incorrect? 

Send a message to our team with photos to the following e-mail address: manon@lepetitolivier.fr 

4. Products 

Where are your products made? 

All our products are made in France, with the exception of the Aleppo Soap. 

Are your products tested on animals? 

In accordance with current regulations, none of our products are tested on animals. Le Petit Olivier has always placed respect for animal welfare at the heart of its commitments. We also prohibit the use of ingredients of animal origin, with the exception of beehive products. What's more, we require our suppliers to certify that all our raw materials have not been tested on animals. 

Why do your products no longer carry the One Voice label? 

Le Petit Olivier has been a "One Voice" partner since its inception. However, French regulations now forbid the use of logos or statements affirming the absence of animal testing, since such tests are prohibited in cosmetics by law. The withdrawal of the label in no way calls into question our commitment: we remain faithful to our values and always ask our suppliers to certify that all our raw materials have not been tested on animals. 

Are your products vegan? 

We prefer ingredients of natural origin and use no animal products in our products, with the exception of beeswax and honey. 

Are your products natural? 

Our products are formulated according to an exacting formulation charter, which you can view in full transparency on a dedicated page on our website. Our products contain a high percentage of ingredients of natural origin. 

Are your products well rated? 

You can find the rating of our products on the applications. For greater convenience, you can consult the Yuka rating of our products directly on the product sheet. 

Where can I find Le Petit Olivier products? 

Le Petit Olivier does not yet have its own stores. However, you can find our products at our official retailers, including almost all supermarkets in France. If in doubt, don't hesitate to contact us. 

5. Customer account 

How do I track my order? 

As soon as your parcel has been shipped, you will receive an e-mail notification including a link enabling you to track its progress. 

What do I do if I've forgotten my account password? 

If you've forgotten your password, simply click on "Forgotten password" when logging in to your account, then enter your email address. A reset link will then be emailed to you. Once you've received the email, click on it to proceed with changing your password. 

How can I change my contact details? 

Log in to your account by clicking on "My account" and entering your e-mail address and password. Click on "My information" and change your contact details.

This Storage Tin is made from durable metal with hinged lids. product.detailed_description: Our latest addition of stoneware is this stunning Indigo 30cm Mixing Bowl, from the Tala Indigo and Ivory range. Thoughtful touches include the Tala brand name embossed around the rim, evoking feelings of nostalgia with the vintage design. The wide rim allows plenty of room to mix ingredients thoroughly inside this bowl. A Natural Corn flour design around the body of the bowl is also one of its main features, both attractive and enhancing the trend of natural products, health and well-being. The textured design also aids firm grip. These bowls are the highest quality of stoneware, which won't chip and will last you a lifetime.

product.ingredients: Carbonated Spring Water, Sicilian Lemon Juice from Concentrate (11%), Comminuted Sicilian Lemon (5%), Sugar, Flavourings, Acid: Citric Acid, Sweetener: Steviol Glycosides
product.features: Refreshingly Light, No Artificial Sweeteners, Colours or Flavourings
product.detailed_description: Our Sparkling Sicilian Lemon is a refreshingly light choice, blending low-calorie carbonated spring water with zesty lemon and a hint of sweetness. This speciality drink revitalises with its bright, sharp notes. M&S UPC - 29372720
product.brand_marketing: M&S Food has been at the heart of the nation since 1884. Giving our customers their best-loved products at the incredible quality and value that only M&S can deliver. From Percy Pig to the freshest M&S Select Farms produce, we grow, source, and develop our own products to give you family-ready food that's unbeatable on flavour and innovation. And that's whether you come to us for your family favourites, an indulgent treat, or your perfect party food spread. After all, this is not just food… This is M&S Food.

###

What range of AVEENO ® should I be using?

Image: flat-lat-2 
The AVEENO^{®} Daily Moisturising Range (green) is formulated to nourish and protect normal to dry skin.
The AVEENO^{®} Skin Relief Range (dark blue) will moisturise and cleanse to help heal dry, irritable skin
The AVEENO^{®} Dermexa Range (light blue) is for very dry itchy skin, and is also suitable for people who may be prone to eczema
###

What are some good tips for dry skincare?

Image: skin microbiome diagram 1 
Your skin draws moisture from the environment, your diet and your skincare routine. The water content of the outermost layer of your skin (the epidermis) also tends to reflect the level of humidity around it, so following the same skincare routine year-round may not be working when the humidity drops.

Here are a few simple ways to keep your skin hydrated and combat dry, itchy skin:
  * Limit time in the shower or bath, we recommend 5-10 minutes.

  * Moisturise immediately after washing. This gives the highest chance of trapping existing moisture in your skin.

  * Using a humidifier will help add much-needed moisture to the air.

  * Choosing fabrics such as cotton and silk, that will allow your skin to breathe.

  * Make sure to include lots of healthy fats like fish, walnuts, olive oil and avocados in your diet, as well as drinking lots of water.
###

What are the skincare benefits of oat?

Image: aveen woman back 1 
Aveeno harnesses the power of the oat through many ways:

Oat Extract/Oat Essence (liquid produced from the oat plant) is naturally rich in Avenanthramides, which are known for their soothing and potent antioxidant properties.

Colloidal Oatmeal (a powder produced by the fine grinding of oats) has moisturising properties that help prevent water loss from the skin.
Oat Oil (a liquid extracted from oat grain) is naturally rich in lips which are essential components for a proper functioning skin barrier.
###

Is AVEENO ® suitable for eczema-prone skin?

Our Dermexa Range is formulated for very dry itchy skin, and is also suitable for eczema- prone skin.

Image 
Image 
Image ###

What are prebiotics and probiotics?

Although they sound pretty similar, probiotics and prebiotics are two vastly different things with specific functions. Probiotics are living microorganisms that are found both naturally in your body and in food and supplements. When consumed or applied to the skin, they provide a wealth of positive benefits for the body, including:

  * Promoting good gut health

  * Strengthening skin overall
Prebiotics on the other hand aren’t actually alive. They are non-digestible ingredients that help to nourish the good bacteria in your gut or on your skin and balance the microbiome.

When probiotics and prebiotics are combined, whether that be in skin cream or in foods, they join forces to become what’s known as a synbiotic. Common synbiotics include supplements, additives and certain foods like yoghurt and cheese.
###

What is the skin microbiome?

Your skin’s microbiome is the collective name for the ecosystem of tiny microorganisms that live on and beneath the surface of your skin. It’s made up of a diverse range of different organisms playing different roles, including:

  * Bacteria – A variety of microscopic organisms which can be both potentially harmful and beneficial to the health of your skin

  * Fungi – Microbes that can be harmful or helpful, a heavy build-up can cause fungal infections
  * Mites – Insect-like microorganisms, invisible to the human eye, that can cause irritation in large numbers

  * Viruses – Microscopic molecules that, if allowed to multiply, can cause infection or illness on the skin
###

Is Aveeno gluten free?

We are unable to recommend AVEENO^{®} products for coeliacs since we cannot confirm the complete absence of gluten in our oat ingredients.

###

What is Aveeno Skin Renewal?

The Aveeno^{®} Skin Renewal Body Range has been formulated to address rough & bumpy skin, uneven tone and loss of firmness concerns. Even more importantly, the products are formulated for sensitive skin.
The range comprising of a Gentle Scrub , Smoothing Cream and Firming Lotion is formulated with nourishing oat known to help support the microbiome and naturally derived PHA: a combination of ingredients selected specifically with sensitive skin in mind. The naturally derived PHA was selected due to its larger molecule size, which doesn’t penetrate the skin as deeply & is therefore more suitable for sensitive skin than other skincare acid groups (AHA’s, BHA’s).
###

Who is Aveeno Skin Renewal for?

The Aveeno Skin Renewal range is formulated for those with dry, sensitive skin. There are three products in the range with different benefits:

  * •Gentle Body Scrub: A precursor to either the Smoothing Cream or Firming Lotion. Formulated with prebiotic oat + niacinamide + naturally derived PHA to get rid of dead skin build-up. Helping to boost skin's natural renewal process through gentle exfoliation. Ensuring skin is ready for smoothing or firming.
  * •Smoothing Cream: Formulated with prebiotic oat + niacinamide + naturally derived PHA to leave dry, rough & bumpy skin feeling smoothed, soft and moisturised in just one night. Also suitable for people with Keratosis Pilaris
  * •Firming Lotion: clinically-proven to moisturise and improve skin elasticity in dry, unfirm and uneven skin. As well as nourishing oat and naturally derived PHA, it contains blackberry leaf extract, known to help enhance collagen and elastin recovery, and can help protect against premature ageing.
###

What is PHA? Are PHA’s good for the skin

Polyhydroxy acids (PHAs) are a popular skincare ingredient that have a wide range of benefits including moisturisation, renewal, and  can enhace stratum corneum barrier function . PHAs can also be better for sensitive skin than other commonly used chemical exfoliants, such as AHAS and BHAs, as they have a larger molecular structure so don’t penetrate as deeply into the skin.

For more information on PHAs see here ###

What other key ingredients are in skin renewal

All three products in the range contain both Nourishing Oat & Naturally Derived PHA to help support the skins microbiome and promote skin renewal for improved tone & texture.

Both the Gentle Body Scrub & Smoothing Cream also contain niacinamide which is known to help brighten skin & reduce discoloration. Whilst the Gentle Body Scrub also contains naturally derived beads, and helps promote skin cell turnover.
The Firming Lotion contains Blackberry Leaf Extract known to help enhance collagen & elastin recovery.
###

Is Skin Renewal suitable for sensitive skin?

Skin Renewal is formulated for sensitive skin. Featuring both nourishing oat & naturally derived PHA. Ingredients known to be gentler on sensitive skin types. Read more about PHA here .

###

Is Skin Renewal dermatologist tested?

All three products in the Skin Renewal range are dermatologist tested.
###

How often should I use skin renewal?

The Gentle Body Scrub can be used 1-2 times per week and can be incorporated into usual shower or bath regime. The Smoothing Cream or Firming Lotion can be used daily to help smooth, moisturise or firm skin.
###

How to apply skin renewal?

 Gentle Body Scrub

Apply a generous amount onto dry or damp skin and massage in circular motions, paying particular attention to dry and rough areas such as elbows, knees and heels. Rinse off with water. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.

 Smoothing Cream

Apply liberally all over body to leave your skin feeling smooth & moisturised. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.

 Firming Lotion
Use daily to moisturise & visibly firm. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.
###

Is Skin Renewal fragrance free?

All three Skin Renewal products are fragrance free.

product.further_description: Deliciously healthy food Best enjoyed as part of a healthy lifestyle & a balanced varied diet. Eat a healthy variety of differently coloured vegetables and fruits each day - at least portions.
product.brand_marketing: M&S Food has been at the heart of the nation since 1884. Giving our customers their best-loved products at the incredible quality and value that only M&S can deliver. From Percy Pig to the freshest M&S Select Farms produce, we grow, source, and develop our own products to give you family-ready food that's unbeatable on flavour and innovation. And that's whether you come to us for your family favourites, an indulgent treat, or your perfect party food spread. After all, this is not just food… This is M&S Food.
product.other_information: Full Product Name: A pasteurised smoothie made from banana, apple and strawberry purées, cherry and apple juices with coconut milk and oat drink with added vitamin B6, D, B12 and Thiamin Storage: Not suitable for freezing. effectiveness
are method products effective against COVID-19 (coronavirus)?
we have not tested our products against SARS-CoV-2 (the strain of Coronavirus causing COVID-19) therefore we are unable to say if our products would effectively kill the virus.
none of our products contain large enough amounts of alcohol to make them a disinfectant. but what we do know is that cleaning removes germs and dirt, lowering the number of them and therefore reducing the risk of spreading infection. rest assured we are monitoring the official research and advice from the World Health Organisation, NHS and UK government about the role of personal hygiene and cleaning products against COVID-19.
home cleaning
our cleaning products are designed for daily use, alongside our anti-bac range for targeted cleaning. only our anti-bac range is proven to kill 99.9% of bacteria. it has also been tested on the H1N1 flu virus, Enterococcus Hirae, Staphylococcus Aureus, E-Coli + Pseudomonas Aeruginosa. however, this does not provide any proof of working against other viruses. none of our products contain chlorine bleach and we do not have a bleach product as we have not found an alternative which meets our health and environmental standards.
hand soap
the latest advice from the World Health Organisation (WHO) is to wash your hands with plain soap and water or use an alcohol rub often, for at least 20 seconds, and avoid touching your eyes, mouth and nose to prevent the spread of infection. according to WHO, washing your bare hands often provides more protection than wearing rubber gloves. you can use any of our hand soaps (gel or foaming) with water to do this.
please note, we do not recommend using our household sprays on your hands. washing-up liquid can be used but is not recommended as it is likely to dry out your hands much quicker than a hand soap. we do not currently have any plans to produce a hand sanitiser, however, we are monitoring demand for this.
dishwashing
like with hand soap, the goal of washing is to remove the virus rather than to destroy it. the latest advice from the UK government is to use a dishwasher (if available) to clean and dry your used crockery and cutlery. if this is not possible, wash them by hand using detergent and warm water and dry them thoroughly using a separate tea towel to prevent the spread of infection. you can use our sister company, Ecover’s dishwasher tablets or any of our washing-up liquids to do this. for more information,
click here
.
laundry
there is a big difference between your day to day routine and what is required when you have an ill person in your house. to the best of our knowledge, washing your clothes more often is not a measure recommended by the World Health Organisation. generally, it is recommended to use a washing powder containing bleach and wash at 60°C to effectively kill bacteria and for the destruction of viruses. you can use Ecover’s washing powder and/or laundry bleach for this.
are method products disinfecting?
disinfectants are products that have a proven effect on the destruction of certain pathogens. none of our products contain large enough amounts of alcohol to make them a disinfectant.
are method products anti-viral?
only our anti-bac range is anti-viral. this was only tested regarding H1N1 flu virus and does not provide any proof of working against other viruses such as SARS-CoV-2 (the strain of Coronavirus causing COVID-19).
are method products anti-bacterial?
our multi-surface cleaners will have some anti-bacterial properties. the surfactants in the daily range will kill some bacteria, for example. but our anti-bac range has been proven to kill 99.9% of bacteria due to the higher concentration of lactic acid. our daily range is more appropriate for everyday use.
are method products anti-microbial?
only our anti-bac range is anti-microbial. it has been tested on the H1N1 flu virus, enterococcus hirae, staphylococcus aureus, e coli + pseudomonas aeruginosa.

why have you partnered with Sarah Story?
as a well renowned dj and radio presenter who champions new dance music and
