Where is my delivery?
Orders can take up to 5 working days to be delivered.
If your item has still not arrived within this time and your tracking information has not updated, please
contact
us and we will look into the status of your delivery.
Can I track my order?
Once your order has been arranged for dispatch, you will receive an email confirmation which will include your tracking number and the name of the courier delivering your parcel. To track your order, you will need to go to the courier website and track the parcel by using your unique tracking number that has been provided on the email.
What is the delivery time?
Orders are delivered within 5 working days, however, this may be extended during our busier periods such as Christmas.
Which couriers do you use?
The majority of orders are delivered via Evri or DPD.
How much is delivery?
Standard delivery to mainland UK is £3.95 and is free for orders over £30.00.
We are able to deliver small parts to Ireland, the ROI and some remote areas. If you need a quote for this service, please directly contact our customer service team on 01656 664483, and they will be able to provide you with a cost for the delivery.
Do you offer a next day delivery service?
Unfortunately, we currently only offer a standard delivery service, however we aim to deliver orders as soon as possible.
Can I change my delivery address once I have placed my order?
Unfortunately, once an order has been confirmed, we are unable to make amendments on any information provided; however, if an order has not yet been dispatched, we can change the address manually to ensure it is delivered to the correct address. On some occasions, it may also be possible to change a delivery address with the courier once an order has already been dispatched but this is not always possible.
If you need to change your address, we would advise contacting our customer service team directly on 0800 515 300 as soon as possible.
Why is my order being returned?
Your order will be returned to us if the information is incorrect or if the courier has not been able to deliver your parcel after multiple attempts and no contact was possible. If your tracking shows your order is being returned to us, please
contact
us and we will be happy to assist.
My order arrived damaged. What are my options?
We’re sorry to learn that your order has arrived damaged. Please send an image of the damaged item(s) to info@addis.co.uk and we will look into resolving the issue as soon as possible. Please use the subject of the email to note your order number.
My order is incorrect? What should I do?
We’re sorry to learn that your order is incorrect. Please send an image of the incorrect item(s) to info@addis.co.uk and we will look into resolving the issue as soon as possible. Please use the subject of the email to note your order number.
My order is missing an item. Is it being sent separately?
We’re sorry to learn that your order is missing an item. Please send an image of your dispatch note to info@addis.co.uk and advise which item is missing from your order. Once this is received, our customer service team will look to resolve the issue for you as soon as possible.
What if I'm not home when delivery is attempted?
If you’re not home when a delivery is attempted, the courier will normally put a note through your letterbox to advise a delivery attempt had been made, and they will try to deliver the following working day. After multiple attempts without success, the courier will either deliver the order to your neighbour or they will arrange for the parcel(s) to be sent back to us. If your tracking shows your order is being returned to us, please
contact
us and we will be happy to assist.
What if my delivery is delayed?
Unfortunately, there are various circumstances that can cause delays. The couriers will normally keep you updated with any delays via the parcel tracking facility; however, if the status of the delivery has not been updated by the courier for 48 hours, please
contact
us and we will be happy to assist.
Where are your products manufactured?
We are a British brand, and a large number of our products are made in the UK; however, there are certain products/materials that have to be sourced outside of the UK for various reasons. Please rest assured we meet all international guidelines to ensure all staff are treated fairly. The manufacturing facilities are fully compliant and pass regular external social and ethical audits, including audits accredited by Sedex, which are monitored annually to ensure we exceed the required standards.
To clarify, external audits include BSCI, Sedex, Smeta and ISO9000 and ISO9001.
I've lost my product manual. Can I obtain a copy?
The majority of our product manuals are stored digitally, therefore please
contact
us with the product manual you require and we will send this to you via email.
Do your products contain BPA?
All of our products that come directly into contact with food are BPA free.
I have removed the label from my product and it has left residue. How do I remove it without damaging the product?
We recommend using a non-abrasive cloth with alcohol, lemon juice, or olive oil to remove residue left from the glue.
What size bin liner do I need?
The liners that we have available have been specifically designed for some of our bins. Please see below:
– 517536 compost liners – suitable for use with all of our compost and kitchen caddies
– 518023 30L bin liners – suitable for our 30L round metal bins which include 518831, 518832, 516179, 515783, 518682, 518017.
– 518024 50L bin liners – designed solely for use with our 50L pedal bins
– 504870 90L degradable refuse sacks – for use with our 90L outdoor dustbins
If we do not have a liner that is suitable for your bin, we recommend purchasing liners that are at least one size larger than the capacity of the bin you have. The reason for this is because the majority of standard liners available in most supermarkets have been designed for cylindrical bins, therefore a 30L liner for a 30L rectangular bin would not be compatible.
Why are my 30L bin liners not suitable for my 30L bin?
The majority of standard liners available in most supermarkets have been designed for cylindrical bins, therefore if you have a rectangular bin or a bin that is not cylindrical, the liners will not be compatible. Due to this, we recommend purchasing liners that are at least one size larger than the capacity of the bin you have.
What do I need to consider when using my rotary airer?
Prior to installing your airer, it is important to ensure that a suitable location for the airer is established to make sure the rotary has room to rotate freely once the arms are extended.
External influences can also affect the resistance of our rotary airers; therefore, we would advise the following:
– When the airer is not in use, fold the item down as this will keep it protected against the elements. If your airer is supplied with a line tidy strap, we would also recommend using this when the airer is not in use, as it will provide extra security.
– Prior to unfolding your airer, please ensure none of the line is tangled around any of the arms
– It is vital not to use your rotary airer in heavy winds. Damage resulting from use in heavy winds can void your guarantee.
– Please do not exceed the maximum weight capacity for you airer, as doing so may result in damage. It is also important to evenly distribute the weight, therefore do not place a heavy duvet on the airer as this will result in too much weight on one side of the airer.
How do I install the ground spike for my rotary airer?
Installing directly into the ground
Place the ground socket in a vertical positioning, maintaining this position at all times. We strongly advise using a flat block of wood to hammer the ground socket into the ground with a mallet. This will protect the socket and maintain its shape.
Installing in concrete (highly recommended)
Dig a hole around 50cm deep and 20cm square. Fill in part of the hole with your concrete mix and place the ground socket vertically in the centre. Continue to pour the rest of the concrete into the hole, ensuring the socket is held in an upright position. Allow this to set for around 48 hours before use.
You should ensure that a suitable location for the airer is established, making sure the rotary has room to rotate freely once the arms are fully extended.
How do I know which ironing board cover I need?
Our Deluxe and Shirtmaster ironing boards have replacement covers that have been specifically designed to fit. If you have our Cirrus ironing board, we recommend our easy fit board cover. For all other ironing boards, you will require our medium or large perfect fit covers, which fits boards up to a certain size and can be fitted by using the drawstring provided.
Medium perfect fit cover – fits boards up to w1110mm x d350mm
Large perfect fit cover – fits boards up to w1350mm x d460mm
How do I adjust the tension on my rotary airer?
The instructions will differ depending on which airer you have as some airers will have clips and with others, the line will be tied to the arms. Therefore, we would advise you to
contact
our customer care team and they will be able to send the appropriate instructions for adjusting the line tension.
Is my compost caddy dishwasher safe?
The compost caddy is dishwasher safe; however, we have discovered that after prolonged use in the dishwasher, the lid discolours, therefore we now recommend handwashing the product to prevent any unsightly discolouration to the caddy.
Is the soft touch bowl BPA free?
Yes, the TPR (Thermoplastic rubber) used is the same material that is used in our microwavable range.
Can I cancel my order?
If you want to cancel your order, please contact our consumer customer care team immediately on 0800 515 300 and they will look into the current status of your order. If your parcel has already been arranged for dispatch, it will not be possible to cancel your order. In this instance, we would advise you to refuse the parcel when delivery is attempted and the order will be returned to us. We will then be able to issue a refund for the full amount.
Can I change or amend my order once it has been placed?
Unfortunately, once an order has been confirmed, we are unable to make amendments on any information provided; however, if an order has not yet been dispatched, we can change some information manually.
If you need make changes to your order, please contact our customer service team directly on 0800 515 300 as soon as possible.
Can I pre-order?
Our website will not allow you to add items to the basket that are out of stock, therefore you will not be able to pre-order.
The product I want is more expensive on your website but I would rather purchase directly from you. Are you able to price match?
Products on our website have to be sold at the RRP, not to undercut any of our trade customers, therefore we will not be able to price match.
My delivery address is incorrect. Can I change this?
Unfortunately, once an order has been confirmed, we are unable to make amendments on any information provided; however, if an order has not yet been dispatched, we can change the address manually to ensure it is delivered to the correct address. On some occasions, it may also be possible to change a delivery address with the courier once an order has already been dispatched but this is not always possible.
If you need to change your address, we would advise contacting our customer service team directly on 0800 515 300 as soon as possible.
When will I receive my order confirmation email?
As soon as your order has been placed, you will receive an email confirmation. Please also check your junk folders as our emails may appear there. If you have not received your order confirmation, please
contact
us and we will be able to send a copy.
Do you ship orders internationally?
Unfortunately, we do not ship singular items to consumers internationally; however, if you are a commercial customer interested in us providing you with a quote, please complete our enquiry form (linked below) to speed up the process of your quote, and our International Sales Manager will get in contact with you.
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd6DrXuIfvsoUzQcwRs2PeOI5LANDjbehaNmgabw1GVtae_xQ/viewform?usp=sf_link
For other enquires relating to international commercial orders, please contact our International Sales Manager via email:
intl@addis.co.uk
Can I add an item to my order once it has been placed?
Unfortunately, due to the way our orders are processed, it is not possible to add an item to your order once it has been placed; however, if the order has not yet been packaged, we will be able to place a manual order with free delivery and arrange for both orders to be sent together. As this is time-sensitive, we would advise contacting our consumer services directly on 0800 515 300 at your earliest convenience and we will be able to advise if your request is possible.
Which payment options do you accept for orders?
We currently accept VISA, VISA Electron, MasterCard, Maestro, Diners Club, JCB & PayPal.
Trust Payments is a trusted and secure payment system that we use to make shopping online safe, therefore you can be sure that your card data is secure.
How do I obtain a VAT invoice for my order?
To obtain a VAT invoice, please
contact
us and we will be able to send a copy via email.
My promotion code doesn't work. Can you help?
Promotional codes will be available on our website. Codes found on external sites will not be valid, therefore will not work on our website. If you are having an issue with a code from our website, please
contact
us and we will be happy to assist.
What is your returns policy?
If you are unhappy with your purchase, you have a right to return without reason within 14 days of receipt of goods.
If the item is not damaged and you choose to return, you will be responsible for the cost of returning the package to us. Once the parcel is received, we will issue a full refund, less the delivery charge (if applicable).
Please ensure items are returned to us in their original packaging.
For further information, please see our
delivery & returns
page.
How do I return a product?
We do not require you to arrange the return of items that have arrived faulty/damaged, therefore in this instance, we would kindly ask you to contact our customer service team on 0800 515 300 for a resolution.
If you are choosing to return a product for any other reason, you are responsible for arranging the the return of the parcel, including the charges incurred. Once the parcel is received, a full refund will be issued, less the delivery charge (if applicable).
Please return the products in their original packaging and include your dispatch note.
Can I exchange an item?
Unfortunately, it is not possible to exchange an item, unless you have received a damaged or incorrect item.
How soon will I be refunded after I have returned an item?
Once we have received your returned parcel, the amount will be refunded within 5 working days. Please note the refund will be less the delivery charge (if applicable). Please keep your proof of postage until you have been refunded.
Do I have to return the product in its original packaging?
Yes, the products must be returned in their original packaging. If you have disposed of the outer box, you may use another sturdy box.
How do I become a distributor?
Please
contact
us and we will be able to provide you with information on how to become a distributor.
How do I open a wholesale account?
Please
contact
us and we will be able to provide you with information on how to open a wholesale account.
How long is the guarantee on my product?
The guarantee period varies with different products; however,
all
Addis products are guaranteed against manufacturing defects for a  period of 1 year from the date of purchase. Proof of purchase is required to validate the guarantee and without this, you will not be able to make a claim.
How do I make a claim on a faulty product?
If your product has become faulty and you need to claim under the guarantee, please complete our
complaints
form and we respond to your claim within 5 working days. Proof of purchase is required to validate the guarantee and without this, we will not be able to assist with providing a replacement.
If my claim is valid, what are my options?
Initially, we will look to repair the item and when this is not achievable, we will provide a replacement. In most instances, we are able to replace with the same item you originally purchased, however this is not always possible. If a product has been discontinued or is exclusive to a retailer where we do not hold the stock, we will offer a similar alternative as a replacement.
My product is faulty. Are spare parts available?
We have a number of spares available to purchase or replace as part of your guarantee.
At present, we do not have all available spares on our website, therefore please send an image of your item or of the part you need replacing to info@addis.co.uk and we will advise if the component is available to send to you.
Am I entitled to a guarantee?
Proof of purchase is required to validate the guarantee and without this, you will not be able to make a claim against the guarantee. There are also other factors to consider when making a claim and Addis will only repair/replace items that have become faulty due to a manufacturing defect.
Does my guarantee renew if my product has been repaired/replaced under the guarantee?
The guarantee is supplied with your original purchase and does not renew if the item is repaired or replaced under the guarantee. After your item has been repaired or replaced, the item will remain covered for the period of time remaining on the guarantee from the original purchase date. For example, if you purchased a product on 1st April 2022 with a 10-year guarantee and received a replacement on 21st September 2027, the guarantee supplied with your original purchase would apply to your replacement and would not expire until 1st April 2032. Proof of purchase is required for all claims, therefore please ensure this is retained for the full guarantee period.
What are the guarantee conditions?
The guarantee will commence from the date of purchase and the length of time your product is guaranteed for will depend on the item you have. The guarantee period will be stated on the product packaging, however, if you are unsure and need clarity on the guarantee you are entitled to, please
contact
us and we will be happy to provide you with the information. Proof of purchase is required for all claims and without this to validate your guarantee, we will not be able to assist with a replacement. The guarantee covers any manufacturing defects and does not cover damage resulting from accident, misuse or abuse, lack of reasonable care, or the affixing of any attachment not provided with the product. No responsibility is assumed for any special, incidental, or consequential damages.
I did not purchase my product directly from the Addis website but there is an issue with it. Is the guarantee with Addis or the seller?
Providing you have your proof of purchase to validate the guarantee, you will be entitled to claim against the guarantee, regardless of where the item was purchased. If an issue occurs within the first 30 days, the item will need to be returned to the retailer for a replacement. After 30 days, Addis will look to resolve any issues for you. However, there are certain product guarantees that need to be dealt with by the retailer due to their exclusivity. We would ask you to
contact
us in the first instance with any issues, as we will be able to assist you and provide contact information if necessary.
I received my product as a gift but there is an issue with it. Am I entitled to a repair/replacement?
For claims against the guarantee, proof of purchase is required. If you are able to obtain this from the purchaser, please complete our
complaints
form and we respond to your claim within 5 working days.
My product is out of guarantee but I only need a spare part. Do you sell parts separately?
We have a number of spares available to purchase, however, we currently do not have them available to purchase via our website, therefore please send an image of your item or of the part you need replacing to info@addis.co.uk and we will advise if the component is available to send to you.

FAQ
[image: Flag]
Home
Frequently Asked Questions
Back
Dr. Oetker Frequently Asked Questions
Most Common Questions & Answers
1
Can you tell me if you use any artificial colours in Dr. Oetker Gel Food Colours? Do you use any of the Southampton 6 at all?
We do not use any of the Southampton 6 artificial colours that require the warning on pack in our Dr. Oetker Gel Food Colours.
We only use artificial colours where required to deliver bright colours:
Artificial Colours we do use:
E133 Brilliant Blue
E142 Green S
2
What bloom is your gelatine?
The bloom of our Dr. Oetker Powdered Gelatine is 140-160 bloom. The bloom of our Dr. Oetker Leaf Gelatine is 230.
3
Where are Ristorante products available?
Our stockist list is available here.
4
Why does your Dr. Oetker Ground Arrowroot Sachet say it contains tapioca starch only?
It is very common for Tapioca Starch to be referred to as Ground Arrowroot as it is derived from the same plant - cassava (Manihot esculenta). For more details on this, please see http://www.britannica.com/plant/arrowroot
The product title is Ground Arrowroot as this is what is commonly used in recipes and how it would be listed in the ingredient list of a recipe. They both perform the same but the actual product is Tapioca starch which is why it is declared as such on the ingredient list.
5
Is Dr. Oetker Ristorante Mozzarella pizza suitable for vegetarians?
Yes, our Dr. Oetker Ristorante Mozzarella pizza is suitable for vegetarians.
The other pizzas in the Dr. Oetker range that are suitable for vegetarians are;
Ristorante Pizza Mozzarella Gluten Free
Ristorante Pizza Funghi
Ristorante Pizza Quattro Formaggi
6
Is the cheese used on the Dr. Oetker range of pizzas pasteurised?
Yes, I can confirm that the cheese used on all of the Dr. Oetker pizzas is pasteurised.
7
Do any of the Dr. Oetker range of pizzas contain MSG?
All of the pizzas in the Dr. Oetker range are free from Genetically Modified ingredients.
8
Are Dr. Oetker pizzas nut free?
None of our pizzas contain nuts.
9
Are Dr. Oetker pizzas alcohol free?
We do not use alcohol as an ingredient or in our production process.
10
Are Dr. Oetker vanilla products alcohol free
We use a hydro-alcoholic solvent for the vanilla beans maceration; however we evaporate the ethyl alcohol. From this we obtain a vanilla concentrate which is diluted on invert sugar. We are unable to guarantee that there will be no residual alcohol in the finished product. The amount of alcohol in the finished product may vary, but can be approximately 0.5% or less, as the alcohol evaporates during the production process.
11
Where is Dr. Oetker from?
Dr. Oetker was founded in Bielefeld, Germany in 1891 by Dr. August Oetker.
12
Is Dr. Oetker baking powder gluten free?
Yes, Dr. Oetker baking powder is gluten free. Please see our page which can give you more information: Baking Powder | Home Baking | Dr. Oetker
13
Are Dr. Oetker Gel Food Colours vegan?
Our Dr. Oetker orange, black, green, blue and yellow Gel Food Colours are suitable for vegans. Our violet, pink and red Gel Food Colours are NOT suitable for vegans.
Please see out useful hints and tips for our colour gels - How to Use Food Colouring in Baking | Dr. Oetker
14
Are Dr. Oetker sprinkles gluten free?
Some of our sprinkles are NOT gluten free. Please see here for our individual product information and nutritional advice: Marshmallow Sprinkles | Home Baking | Dr. Oetker
15
Does Dr. Oetker baking powder contain aluminium?
Neither aluminium nor aluminium compounds are added intentionally during the manufacturing process of our Baking Powder.
Baking Powder - Any residual aluminium would be less than 200ppm.
The aluminium content is naturally occurring coming from the raw material.
16
Is Dr. Oetker chocolate gluten free?
Most of our chocolate range is gluten free. However, please check out the individual product information here: Chocolate Inclusions | Home Baking | Dr. Oetker
17
Is Dr. Oetker Halal?
Please follow the link below to search for your favourite product to check if it is Halal: All products | Dr. Oetker
18
Where to buy Dr. Oetker products?
We use a wide range of retailers from Asda, Ocado, Morrisons, Tesco and more. Our products are subject to availability please see individual retailer websites for our stock availability.

L56@P2: • Leather must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible Leather Sourcing Policy
L57@P2: • Animal Fibres (e.g. wool, cashmere) must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible
L58@P2: Wool Sourcing Policy and our Cashmere Code of Practice for animal welfare respectively.

L72@P3: THE FIVE FREEDOMS OF ANIMAL WELFARE
L73@P3: In developing minimum standards for sourcing any animal product Marks & Spencer
L74@P3: consider the internationally recognised “Five Freedoms” as a framework and for guidance. It
L75@P3: is important that the sourcing of any animal derived materials for M&S are underpinned by
L76@P3: these principles:
L77@P3: 1. Freedom from Hunger and Thirst – by ready access to fresh water and a diet to
L78@P3: maintain full health and vigour
L79@P3: 2. Freedom from Discomfort – by providing an appropriate environment including
L80@P3: shelter and a comfortable resting area
L81@P3: 3. Freedom from Pain, Injury and Disease – by prevention or rapid diagnosis and
L82@P3: treatment
L83@P3: 4. Freedom to Express Normal Behaviour – by providing sufficient space, proper
L84@P3: facilities and company of the animal’s own kind
L85@P3: 5. Freedom from Fear and Distress – by ensuring conditions and treatment which
L86@P3: avoid mental suffering
L87@P3: ANIMAL TESTING
L88@P3: Marks and Spencer will not conduct or commission any tests on animals. All M&S own brand
L89@P3: cosmetic and household products and ingredients must be approved by the BUAV under
L90@P3: the Humane Cosmetics Standard, The Leaping Bunny Standard. This standard has been in
L91@P3: place since January 2006

L94@P3: product itself must not compromise the welfare of the animal for which it is intended to be
L95@P3: used, using the Five Freedoms as a reference.

Indulge in everyday luxury as you step out of the bath or shower with this irresistibly soft, silky-smooth towel. Now crafted at an enhanced 650GSM, it delivers an even plusher, more indulgent feel making it our softest Egyptian cotton towel yet, with exceptional absorbency. Expertly woven from premium Egyptian cotton, the long-staple fibres offer outstanding durability, reduced linting and a beautifully silky handle, while helping colours stay rich and vibrant wash after wash. Finished with a modernised border for improved absorbency and twin-needle stitching with a double-stitched hem for added durability, it’s designed to look and feel luxurious for longer. This towel is quick to dry and contains our innovative StayNew™ technology which helps preserve its fresh, as-new appearance.
This towel’s GSM rating is 650 GSM.GSM stands for grams per square metre and indicates the weight and density of the towel. Our towels range from 450-800 GSM. 600-800 GSM signifies a heavier, more luxurious towel. The pile in these deluxe towels is denser and more lavish and resembles the towels you’d find in a luxury hotel.

L75: # TEA LIGHTS IN 100% STEARIN
L76: 
L77: Swedish people use more than 300 million tea lights every year. Therefore, it is important to choose the right candle for health and the environment.
L78: Below you will find answers to the most frequently asked questions about tea lights.
L79: ### MATERIALS
L80: 
L81: What materials are used in Liljeholmens tealights and where are they made?
L82: Liljeholmens tealights are made in Oskarshamn, Sweden, from stearin based only on the renewable raw material tallow. Liljeholmens candles do not contain stearin based on palm oil or palm fats.
L83: You can buy tealights made of different materials - stearin, paraffin, palm oil, and more. What is the difference, and which candle should I choose?
L84: Liljeholmens tealights are made from 100% stearin based solely on the renewable raw material tallow. The tallow is exclusively a residual product that, in this way, gets a second use as a raw material for the production of stearin.
L85: Some tealights of other brands are made of 100% stearin based on palm oil. Palm oil is a controversial product that is resource-efficient, but has gained a bad reputation due to the clearing of rainforests to replace palm oil plantations. If in doubt, ask the manufacturer what the candle contains.
L86: Candles can also be made from paraffin wax, which is a residual oil product - unlike stearin, it is a fossil and finite resource. A paraffin candle, on the other hand, can burn more evenly and is not as sensitive to temperature changes as a candle made of stearin can be. A paraffin candle is therefore more suitable than a candle in an outdoor lantern.
L87: ### CANDLE LEFT IN THE CUP
L88: 
L89: Why is there sometimes stearin left in the cup when the tealight has burnt out?
L90: The burning time of Liljeholmens candles has been carefully tested by our quality department, but the burning time may still differ slightly from the time stated on the packaging. This may be due to the following factors:
L91: •  Candles made of stearin may burn more slowly if the room is cold or if they are placed outside in a lantern during the winter. This is usually because the stearin in the cup does not heat up enough to allow all the stearin in the candle to become hot and liquid - the result can be that the candle only burns down the center of the cup.
L92: •  A tealight holder made of metal or thicker glass and a plate made of stone or other compact material can cause the heat from the candle to be dissipated and therefore burn more poorly and with a lower flame. It is best to try out different types of lanterns, tealight holders, and placements of the tealight to get the best possible conditions for the candle to burn well and safely.
L93: •  All tealights - whatever brand - are designed to be lit only once and then allowed to burn out. Lighting and extinguishing a tealight several times may result in a shorter burning time than specified. If you do this, you should make sure that all the stearin has heated up completely, i.e., is liquid, before you extinguish the candle, a pit may form in the middle of the candle or the wick may be affected in such a way that the flame becomes small and thin.
L94: •  A candle should always be placed on a flat and non-tilted surface. If a tealight is placed on an inclined surface, this can cause the candle to burn unevenly and the stearin does not have time to become hot and liquid during the burning time. There is also a risk that it will be too hot in one part of the cup and that the candle will burn with a higher and stronger flame than normal.
L95: 
L96: • You should always use a holder or heater with adequate ventilation for your tealights.
L97: • It is best to try out different types of lanterns and positions of the tealight under supervision to get the best possible conditions for the candle to burn well and safely.
L98: ### RECYCLING
L99: How should I sort the packaging and the tealight cup once the candle has burnt out?
L100: The cup of the Liljeholmens's tealights is made of aluminum and to recycle aluminum is energy efficient. It is important to sort the aluminium cup and the metal holder for the wick correctly after the tealight has burned out. Separate the cup from the metal holder for the wick and leave both the parts in the metal sorting at your recycling center.
L101: The packaging containing the tea lights is sorted as paper packaging at the recycling station.
L102: ### WHAT SHOULD I CONSIDER WHEN USING TEA LIGHTS?
L103: - Do not leave candles unattended. A good rule is that the person who lit the candles is responsible for them - and puts them out!
L104: - Never leave children or animals alone with candles.
L105: - Always use candle holders. A tealight should be placed in a holder or heater with adequate ventilation.
L106: - Make sure that the candle stands freely, steadily and completely upright both on the base and in the candleholder.
L107: - Think about where you place the candle, so that, for example, a curtain cannot be fluttered by wind or drafts, or that the candle is placed above a combustible material such as a sofa, TV or other electrical appliances.
L108: - Do not place a candle in a draft.
L109: - Do not place candles too close together - at least 7 cm should be left between two lit candles.
L110: - Never blow out the candle - extinguish it by covering it with a candle extinguisher. Never extinguish a candle with liquid!
L111: - Remember not to move your tea light when it is burning. There is a risk that the growth support holding the wick in place in the center of the holder will move, and this can cause the candle to get too hot and the flame to get higher. In this case, extinguish the candle by covering it with a pot lid; for example, do not try to blow out the candle.
L112: - If you have to move the candle, extinguish it first, wait until the stearin has solidified, and then move the candle.
L113: - Always keep the candle free of matches or other debris to avoid the candle flaring up.
L114: Did you not find an answer to your question here? Contact us (info@liljeholmens.se), and we will answer you as soon as possible!

L7@P1: BACKGROUND
L8@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to using responsibly sourced raw materials including the
L9@P1: use of products derived from animals. This policy forms part of our commitment to uphold
L10@P1: the M&S animal welfare principles for all animal derived products we source.
L11@P1: SCOPE
L12@P1: This policy covers products sold in all Clothing, Home and Beauty areas that contain any
L13@P1: animal derived raw materials. The scope includes all main fabrics/textiles, trims,
L14@P1: componentry packaging, chemicals, pigments and dyestuffs.
L15@P1: This policy is intended to complement the additional specific sourcing policies for
L16@P1: Cashmere, Wool, Leather and Feather and Down.
L17@P1: RATONALE AND OBJECTIVES
L18@P1: • To ensure Marks & Spencer meets its long-standing commitment to improve animal
L19@P1: welfare in its supply chains and ensure all animal derived materials are sourced from
L20@P1: farms with good animal welfare practices. Marks & Spencer are committed to
L21@P1: improving animal welfare across our global supply chains and we are working to
L22@P1: source all animal-derived materials from farms with good animal welfare practices
L23@P1: • To lay out a set of uniform principles and guidelines around the sourcing of animal
L24@P1: derived raw materials
L25@P1: • To also ensure that appropriate due diligence is undertaken with regards to the
L26@P1: sourcing of products in relation to animal welfare
L27@P1: M&S MANDATORY PRINCIPLES FOR SOURCING
L28@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to protecting any endangered or vulnerable species and
L29@P1: to the prevention of cruelty. Through our supply chains we seek to promote, encourage and
L30@P1: foster higher animal welfare standards using codes, recommendations and audited supply
L31@P1: chains. We will continuously review our supply chains and where there are practices that
L32@P1: are of concern, we will take a considered course of action.
L33@P1: No animal will be slaughtered specifically for the manufacture or sourcing of M&S products.
L34@P1: PROHIBITED SOURCES
L35@P1: The following materials do not comply with our business principles for animal welfare and
L36@P1: therefore must not be used in any of our non-food products:
L37@P1: • Any material from any endangered species, defined as those which appear on the
L38@P1-2: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) (see www.cites.org/ Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L39@P2: Version Number 2.0 Page 3 of 5
L40@P2: Public Copy
L41@P2: for list of species) or the IUCN red list as Critically Endangered,
L42@P2: Endangered or Vulnerable (www.redlist.org/).
L43@P2: • No animal must be slaughtered specifically to produce any non- food M&S products.
L44@P2: • Fur: this includes farmed fur (e.g. fox, sable, mink, chinchilla, rabbit)
L45@P2: • Angora Rabbit fibre
L46@P2: • Alpaca fibre
L47@P2: • Astrakhan (Karakul) or any other leather/skin products which are the product of
L48@P2: unnatural abortions
L49@P2: • Any material obtained from live skinning (e.g. reptiles) or live boiling
L50@P2: • Any cow hides sourced from India
L51@P2: • Any animal derived bone or horn
L52@P2: • Any down or feathers from exotic birds, including but not limited to ostrich
L53@P2: • Any coral
L54@P2: RESTRICTED SOURCES
L55@P2: The following materials are currently accepted provided minimum requirements are met:
L56@P2: • Leather must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible Leather Sourcing Policy
L57@P2: • Animal Fibres (e.g. wool, cashmere) must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible
L58@P2: Wool Sourcing Policy and our Cashmere Code of Practice for animal welfare respectively.
L59@P2: All wool must be sourced from sheep that have not been mulesed
L60@P2: • Mohair must only be sourced through routes fully certified to the Textile Exchange
L61@P2: Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS)
L62@P2: • Feather and Down must not be obtained from the live plucking of birds or from birds used
L63@P2: in the production of Foie Gras. All Feather and Down must be sourced in compliance to
L64@P2: our Responsible Feather and Down Sourcing Policy
L65@P2: • All other animal derived materials must be sourced in accordance with this policy and
L66@P2: relevant details must be provided on an Animal derived material declaration form
L67@P2: • Any shell from vulnerable or endangered species must not be used (as defined by
L68@P2: CITES/IUCN red list)
L69@P2-3: • Only pearls form cultivated sources are allowed Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L70@P3: Version Number 2.0 Page 4 of 5

L72@P3: THE FIVE FREEDOMS OF ANIMAL WELFARE
L73@P3: In developing minimum standards for sourcing any animal product Marks & Spencer
L74@P3: consider the internationally recognised “Five Freedoms” as a framework and for guidance. It
L75@P3: is important that the sourcing of any animal derived materials for M&S are underpinned by
L76@P3: these principles:
L77@P3: 1. Freedom from Hunger and Thirst – by ready access to fresh water and a diet to
L78@P3: maintain full health and vigour
L79@P3: 2. Freedom from Discomfort – by providing an appropriate environment including
L80@P3: shelter and a comfortable resting area
L81@P3: 3. Freedom from Pain, Injury and Disease – by prevention or rapid diagnosis and
L82@P3: treatment
L83@P3: 4. Freedom to Express Normal Behaviour – by providing sufficient space, proper
L84@P3: facilities and company of the animal’s own kind
L85@P3: 5. Freedom from Fear and Distress – by ensuring conditions and treatment which
L86@P3: avoid mental suffering

L89@P3: cosmetic and household products and ingredients must be approved by the BUAV under

L91@P3: place since January 2006

L94@P3: product itself must not compromise the welfare of the animal for which it is intended to be
L95@P3: used, using the Five Freedoms as a reference.

L102@P3-4: kingdom, that is all vertebrates and multi-cellular invertebrates. The word may be used either Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy

###

What range of AVEENO ® should I be using?

Image: flat-lat-2 
The AVEENO^{®} Daily Moisturising Range (green) is formulated to nourish and protect normal to dry skin.
The AVEENO^{®} Skin Relief Range (dark blue) will moisturise and cleanse to help heal dry, irritable skin
The AVEENO^{®} Dermexa Range (light blue) is for very dry itchy skin, and is also suitable for people who may be prone to eczema
###

What are some good tips for dry skincare?

Image: skin microbiome diagram 1 
Your skin draws moisture from the environment, your diet and your skincare routine. The water content of the outermost layer of your skin (the epidermis) also tends to reflect the level of humidity around it, so following the same skincare routine year-round may not be working when the humidity drops.

Here are a few simple ways to keep your skin hydrated and combat dry, itchy skin:
  * Limit time in the shower or bath, we recommend 5-10 minutes.

  * Moisturise immediately after washing. This gives the highest chance of trapping existing moisture in your skin.

  * Using a humidifier will help add much-needed moisture to the air.

  * Choosing fabrics such as cotton and silk, that will allow your skin to breathe.

  * Make sure to include lots of healthy fats like fish, walnuts, olive oil and avocados in your diet, as well as drinking lots of water.
###

What are the skincare benefits of oat?

Image: aveen woman back 1 
Aveeno harnesses the power of the oat through many ways:

Oat Extract/Oat Essence (liquid produced from the oat plant) is naturally rich in Avenanthramides, which are known for their soothing and potent antioxidant properties.

Colloidal Oatmeal (a powder produced by the fine grinding of oats) has moisturising properties that help prevent water loss from the skin.
Oat Oil (a liquid extracted from oat grain) is naturally rich in lips which are essential components for a proper functioning skin barrier.
###

Is AVEENO ® suitable for eczema-prone skin?

Our Dermexa Range is formulated for very dry itchy skin, and is also suitable for eczema- prone skin.

Image 
Image 
Image ###

What are prebiotics and probiotics?

Although they sound pretty similar, probiotics and prebiotics are two vastly different things with specific functions. Probiotics are living microorganisms that are found both naturally in your body and in food and supplements. When consumed or applied to the skin, they provide a wealth of positive benefits for the body, including:

  * Promoting good gut health

  * Strengthening skin overall
Prebiotics on the other hand aren’t actually alive. They are non-digestible ingredients that help to nourish the good bacteria in your gut or on your skin and balance the microbiome.

When probiotics and prebiotics are combined, whether that be in skin cream or in foods, they join forces to become what’s known as a synbiotic. Common synbiotics include supplements, additives and certain foods like yoghurt and cheese.
###

What is the skin microbiome?

Your skin’s microbiome is the collective name for the ecosystem of tiny microorganisms that live on and beneath the surface of your skin. It’s made up of a diverse range of different organisms playing different roles, including:

  * Bacteria – A variety of microscopic organisms which can be both potentially harmful and beneficial to the health of your skin

  * Fungi – Microbes that can be harmful or helpful, a heavy build-up can cause fungal infections
  * Mites – Insect-like microorganisms, invisible to the human eye, that can cause irritation in large numbers

  * Viruses – Microscopic molecules that, if allowed to multiply, can cause infection or illness on the skin
###

Is Aveeno gluten free?

We are unable to recommend AVEENO^{®} products for coeliacs since we cannot confirm the complete absence of gluten in our oat ingredients.

###

What is Aveeno Skin Renewal?

The Aveeno^{®} Skin Renewal Body Range has been formulated to address rough & bumpy skin, uneven tone and loss of firmness concerns. Even more importantly, the products are formulated for sensitive skin.
The range comprising of a Gentle Scrub , Smoothing Cream and Firming Lotion is formulated with nourishing oat known to help support the microbiome and naturally derived PHA: a combination of ingredients selected specifically with sensitive skin in mind. The naturally derived PHA was selected due to its larger molecule size, which doesn’t penetrate the skin as deeply & is therefore more suitable for sensitive skin than other skincare acid groups (AHA’s, BHA’s).
###

Who is Aveeno Skin Renewal for?

The Aveeno Skin Renewal range is formulated for those with dry, sensitive skin. There are three products in the range with different benefits:

  * •Gentle Body Scrub: A precursor to either the Smoothing Cream or Firming Lotion. Formulated with prebiotic oat + niacinamide + naturally derived PHA to get rid of dead skin build-up. Helping to boost skin's natural renewal process through gentle exfoliation. Ensuring skin is ready for smoothing or firming.
  * •Smoothing Cream: Formulated with prebiotic oat + niacinamide + naturally derived PHA to leave dry, rough & bumpy skin feeling smoothed, soft and moisturised in just one night. Also suitable for people with Keratosis Pilaris
  * •Firming Lotion: clinically-proven to moisturise and improve skin elasticity in dry, unfirm and uneven skin. As well as nourishing oat and naturally derived PHA, it contains blackberry leaf extract, known to help enhance collagen and elastin recovery, and can help protect against premature ageing.
###

What is PHA? Are PHA’s good for the skin

Polyhydroxy acids (PHAs) are a popular skincare ingredient that have a wide range of benefits including moisturisation, renewal, and  can enhace stratum corneum barrier function . PHAs can also be better for sensitive skin than other commonly used chemical exfoliants, such as AHAS and BHAs, as they have a larger molecular structure so don’t penetrate as deeply into the skin.

For more information on PHAs see here ###

What other key ingredients are in skin renewal

All three products in the range contain both Nourishing Oat & Naturally Derived PHA to help support the skins microbiome and promote skin renewal for improved tone & texture.

Both the Gentle Body Scrub & Smoothing Cream also contain niacinamide which is known to help brighten skin & reduce discoloration. Whilst the Gentle Body Scrub also contains naturally derived beads, and helps promote skin cell turnover.
The Firming Lotion contains Blackberry Leaf Extract known to help enhance collagen & elastin recovery.
###

Is Skin Renewal suitable for sensitive skin?

Skin Renewal is formulated for sensitive skin. Featuring both nourishing oat & naturally derived PHA. Ingredients known to be gentler on sensitive skin types. Read more about PHA here .

###

Is Skin Renewal dermatologist tested?

All three products in the Skin Renewal range are dermatologist tested.
###

How often should I use skin renewal?

The Gentle Body Scrub can be used 1-2 times per week and can be incorporated into usual shower or bath regime. The Smoothing Cream or Firming Lotion can be used daily to help smooth, moisturise or firm skin.
###

How to apply skin renewal?

 Gentle Body Scrub

Apply a generous amount onto dry or damp skin and massage in circular motions, paying particular attention to dry and rough areas such as elbows, knees and heels. Rinse off with water. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.

 Smoothing Cream

Apply liberally all over body to leave your skin feeling smooth & moisturised. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.

 Firming Lotion
Use daily to moisturise & visibly firm. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.
###

Is Skin Renewal fragrance free?

All three Skin Renewal products are fragrance free.

L31@P1: chains. We will continuously review our supply chains and where there are practices that

product.name: Fifty Pounds Gin
product.detailed_description: A strikingly smooth London Dry Gin. Fifty Pounds Gin is a handcrafted London Dry Gin, triple filtered for remarkable smoothness. The brand takes its name from the 1736 Gin Act which imposed an annual license fee of Fifty Pounds on those wishing to produce and sell gin. This Act was a (failed) attempt to curb the prevalent gin craze. The bottle is based on the ‘case gin’ design of that Georgian era; tapered to allow tight end packing in a pre-bubble wrap time. Each bottle of Fifty Pounds Gin also bears its individual distillation batch number, together with the year that it was distilled. Please drink responsibly: The UK Chief Medical Officers recommend adults do not regularly drink more than 14 units per week
product.brand_marketing: In 1736, during the reign of George II of England, an annual levy of 50 pounds, known as the 1736 Gin Act, was imposed on those wishing to produce and sell gin. Only two distilleries agreed to pay this tax...

Trustpilot ## ABOUT US

Many of you will be aware of Cocopup's sister brand, Coconut Lane! Continually inspired by trend-led, instagrammable designs, Coconut Lane was founded in 2015 by BFFs Charlie and Jess.

Both being dog OBSESSED, lockdown 2020 was the perfect excuse to finally fulfil the dream of getting a dog! There were accessories to choose from on the market,  but finding accessories that were fun, aesthetic and allowed Jess to match Ralph (our cheeky CEO Cavachon) was a challenge...
One day, Jess & Charlie were having a coffee in Coconut Lane's office thinking about what new products to branch into next. Ralph was running around shredding cardboard all over the office floor and having fully established himself as our HQ pup, the idea of a dog brand felt like the perfect new venture! So Cocopup was born and the rest is history!

Image We wanted to create a brand all about matching accessories in the cutest patterns for you and your bestie! We wanted a stylish, yet practical bag that could be used for dog walks..or for brunch! The Cocopup Dog Walking Bag was born..designed and created by us, with in-built poop bag holder, so much space for all your dog walk needs PLUS interchangeable straps for you to match with your pups harness - it's a dog mum dream!
Since then, our ranges and designs have continued to grow and grow! We have launched multiple new designs and products since starting the brand, and this is just the beginning!

Image 
Image 
Image Cocopup and Coconut Lane are run by a small, close knit team of 14 women working hard split across both brands. We love to work hard as a team, but also play hard and love a team outing! Vanessa is our star baker and we love a team catch up with a cuppa and some cake! (whilst being forced into filming Tiktok's by Char & Imi!)

Make sure you are following our Instagram and Tiktok @cocopupuk for all the BTS content of office life at Coco HQ!
## MEET RALPH

We also couldn't introduce our brand without giving a very special mention to our very spoilt office pooch Ralphie. Like so many people in 2020, Jess went on the hunt for a lockdown companion.

Ralph is a cheeky little Cavachon, loves stealing socks, being a grumpy old man sometimes, playing with his fave toy Hedgehog and finding things he's not allowed to chew on.

We're so grateful to our little cheeky Ralph as we wouldn't be here without him!

Cruelty Free
5 FACTS ABOUT
OLAY'S PUSH FOR CRUELTY-FREE SKIN CARE
IN THE INDUSTRY
Fact 1
WHAT WE BELIEVE
Olay is calling for an end to animal testing in skin care and the beauty industry.
Fact 2
CHANGING THE BEAUTY INDUSTRY
We do not test our products on animals. Olay is working closely with governments around the world to provide alternative research methods to eliminate testing on animals, enabling cruelty-free skin care in the beauty industry. For example, in a few countries where Olay is sold, governments still mandate animal tests. In those cases, Olay can be required by law to submit our products to labs where we know animal tests are happening.
This is why we do not claim cruelty-free on our packaging. We do not believe these tests are necessary to evaluate safety or performance. But today, they won’t accept alternative non-animal testing methods. We remain steadfast and will continue to advocate for alternative methods to end animal tests in the industry.
Fact 3
HOW TO TEST OUR PRODUCTS
Olay tests its products on “lab skins,” including unique, Olay-invented versions that have the same physical properties as natural skin but are created wholly in a lab setting from non-animal materials. Testing on lab skin helps ensure our products work as intended and are safe to use. We also research our products with thousands of women around the world to ensure they provide real, transformational skincare benefits that women expect when using Olay.
Fact 4
INVESTING IN CRUELTY-FREE RESEARCH
Olay's parent company, P&G, has devoted a total of more than $480 million to develop cruelty-free alternatives. Additionally, P&G has joined industry coalitions to share research and testing methodologies so that other skin care brands and the industry-at-large can end animal testing and move toward cruelty-free skin care.
Fact 5
PARTNERING WITH THE HUMANE SOCIETY
For more than 20 years, the Humane Society family of organizations has collaborated with Procter & Gamble to advance the development and regulatory acceptance of non-animal testing approaches. We are excited to welcome P&G as an official supporter of our #BeCrueltyFree campaign to achieve a legislative end to cosmetic animal testing and trade in all major cosmetic markets worldwide.
Troy Seidle,
Vice President of the Humane Society International

L4@P0-1: ANIMAL WELFARE POLICYLatest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L5@P1: Version Number 2.0 Page 2 of 5
L6@P1: Public Copy
L7@P1: BACKGROUND
L8@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to using responsibly sourced raw materials including the
L9@P1: use of products derived from animals. This policy forms part of our commitment to uphold
L10@P1: the M&S animal welfare principles for all animal derived products we source.
L11@P1: SCOPE
L12@P1: This policy covers products sold in all Clothing, Home and Beauty areas that contain any
L13@P1: animal derived raw materials. The scope includes all main fabrics/textiles, trims,
L14@P1: componentry packaging, chemicals, pigments and dyestuffs.
L15@P1: This policy is intended to complement the additional specific sourcing policies for
L16@P1: Cashmere, Wool, Leather and Feather and Down.
L17@P1: RATONALE AND OBJECTIVES
L18@P1: • To ensure Marks & Spencer meets its long-standing commitment to improve animal
L19@P1: welfare in its supply chains and ensure all animal derived materials are sourced from
L20@P1: farms with good animal welfare practices. Marks & Spencer are committed to
L21@P1: improving animal welfare across our global supply chains and we are working to
L22@P1: source all animal-derived materials from farms with good animal welfare practices
L23@P1: • To lay out a set of uniform principles and guidelines around the sourcing of animal
L24@P1: derived raw materials
L25@P1: • To also ensure that appropriate due diligence is undertaken with regards to the
L26@P1: sourcing of products in relation to animal welfare
L27@P1: M&S MANDATORY PRINCIPLES FOR SOURCING
L28@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to protecting any endangered or vulnerable species and
L29@P1: to the prevention of cruelty. Through our supply chains we seek to promote, encourage and
L30@P1: foster higher animal welfare standards using codes, recommendations and audited supply
L31@P1: chains. We will continuously review our supply chains and where there are practices that
L32@P1: are of concern, we will take a considered course of action.
L33@P1: No animal will be slaughtered specifically for the manufacture or sourcing of M&S products.
L34@P1: PROHIBITED SOURCES
L35@P1: The following materials do not comply with our business principles for animal welfare and
L36@P1: therefore must not be used in any of our non-food products:
L37@P1: • Any material from any endangered species, defined as those which appear on the
L38@P1-2: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) (see www.cites.org/ Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L39@P2: Version Number 2.0 Page 3 of 5
L40@P2: Public Copy
L41@P2: for list of species) or the IUCN red list as Critically Endangered,
L42@P2: Endangered or Vulnerable (www.redlist.org/).
L43@P2: • No animal must be slaughtered specifically to produce any non- food M&S products.
L44@P2: • Fur: this includes farmed fur (e.g. fox, sable, mink, chinchilla, rabbit)
L45@P2: • Angora Rabbit fibre
L46@P2: • Alpaca fibre
L47@P2: • Astrakhan (Karakul) or any other leather/skin products which are the product of
L48@P2: unnatural abortions
L49@P2: • Any material obtained from live skinning (e.g. reptiles) or live boiling
L50@P2: • Any cow hides sourced from India
L51@P2: • Any animal derived bone or horn
L52@P2: • Any down or feathers from exotic birds, including but not limited to ostrich
L53@P2: • Any coral
L54@P2: RESTRICTED SOURCES
L55@P2: The following materials are currently accepted provided minimum requirements are met:
L56@P2: • Leather must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible Leather Sourcing Policy
L57@P2: • Animal Fibres (e.g. wool, cashmere) must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible
L58@P2: Wool Sourcing Policy and our Cashmere Code of Practice for animal welfare respectively.
L59@P2: All wool must be sourced from sheep that have not been mulesed
L60@P2: • Mohair must only be sourced through routes fully certified to the Textile Exchange
L61@P2: Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS)
L62@P2: • Feather and Down must not be obtained from the live plucking of birds or from birds used
L63@P2: in the production of Foie Gras. All Feather and Down must be sourced in compliance to
L64@P2: our Responsible Feather and Down Sourcing Policy
L65@P2: • All other animal derived materials must be sourced in accordance with this policy and
L66@P2: relevant details must be provided on an Animal derived material declaration form
L67@P2: • Any shell from vulnerable or endangered species must not be used (as defined by
L68@P2: CITES/IUCN red list)
L69@P2-3: • Only pearls form cultivated sources are allowed Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L70@P3: Version Number 2.0 Page 4 of 5
L71@P3: Public Copy
L72@P3: THE FIVE FREEDOMS OF ANIMAL WELFARE
L73@P3: In developing minimum standards for sourcing any animal product Marks & Spencer
L74@P3: consider the internationally recognised “Five Freedoms” as a framework and for guidance. It
L75@P3: is important that the sourcing of any animal derived materials for M&S are underpinned by
L76@P3: these principles:
L77@P3: 1. Freedom from Hunger and Thirst – by ready access to fresh water and a diet to
L78@P3: maintain full health and vigour
L79@P3: 2. Freedom from Discomfort – by providing an appropriate environment including
L80@P3: shelter and a comfortable resting area
L81@P3: 3. Freedom from Pain, Injury and Disease – by prevention or rapid diagnosis and
L82@P3: treatment
L83@P3: 4. Freedom to Express Normal Behaviour – by providing sufficient space, proper
L84@P3: facilities and company of the animal’s own kind
L85@P3: 5. Freedom from Fear and Distress – by ensuring conditions and treatment which
L86@P3: avoid mental suffering
L87@P3: ANIMAL TESTING
L88@P3: Marks and Spencer will not conduct or commission any tests on animals. All M&S own brand
L89@P3: cosmetic and household products and ingredients must be approved by the BUAV under
L90@P3: the Humane Cosmetics Standard, The Leaping Bunny Standard. This standard has been in
L91@P3: place since January 2006
L92@P3: PET ACCESSORIES
L93@P3: Any pet accessories are subject to all mandatory principles for sourcing. In addition, the
L94@P3: product itself must not compromise the welfare of the animal for which it is intended to be
L95@P3: used, using the Five Freedoms as a reference.
L96@P3: PRODUCT PROMOTION
L97@P3: Marks and Spencer will review all animal imagery used in the promotion of its products to
L98@P3: ensure that it does not endorse animal exploitation, cruelty or irresponsible use or
L99@P3: ownership.
L100@P3: DEFINITIONS
L101@P3: Animals: The Vegan Society understands the word animal to refer to the entire animal
L102@P3-4: kingdom, that is all vertebrates and multi-cellular invertebrates. The word may be used either Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L103@P4: Version Number 2.0 Page 5 of 5
L104@P4: Public Copy
L105@P4: as a noun or an adjective and to refer to a species, or an individual animal,
L106@P4: depending on context.
L107@P4: Animal derived materials: Materials including ingredients that have an animal (see above
L108@P4: definition), origin, regardless of whether they have been harvested form live or dead
L109@P4: animals.

# FAQ's
### I cannot see pricing or add items to my cart....

You will need to be a trade customer and logged in, in order to see our trade prices and be able to order items. We are a supplier to the toy & gift trade and supply wholesale quantities to businesses in the UK and Ireland. We are unable to supply direct to the consumer.
### I have completed the account registration form but have not heard back....

Please note that customer authentication is a manual process carried out by our team. In most cases this will be handled as a matter of priority, within normal working hours only.
### I am a retail customer - where can I find KidAntics products for sale?

Many online, high street stores or gift shops stock our products. If you search for our products in your search engine of choice, you should find some suitable retailers.

If you struggle, or prefer to support more local businesses, please contact us , stating your location and we should be able to let you know your local stockist(s).

###

What range of AVEENO ® should I be using?

Image: flat-lat-2 
The AVEENO^{®} Daily Moisturising Range (green) is formulated to nourish and protect normal to dry skin.
The AVEENO^{®} Skin Relief Range (dark blue) will moisturise and cleanse to help heal dry, irritable skin
The AVEENO^{®} Dermexa Range (light blue) is for very dry itchy skin, and is also suitable for people who may be prone to eczema
###

What are some good tips for dry skincare?

Image: skin microbiome diagram 1 
Your skin draws moisture from the environment, your diet and your skincare routine. The water content of the outermost layer of your skin (the epidermis) also tends to reflect the level of humidity around it, so following the same skincare routine year-round may not be working when the humidity drops.

Here are a few simple ways to keep your skin hydrated and combat dry, itchy skin:
  * Limit time in the shower or bath, we recommend 5-10 minutes.

  * Moisturise immediately after washing. This gives the highest chance of trapping existing moisture in your skin.

  * Using a humidifier will help add much-needed moisture to the air.

  * Choosing fabrics such as cotton and silk, that will allow your skin to breathe.

  * Make sure to include lots of healthy fats like fish, walnuts, olive oil and avocados in your diet, as well as drinking lots of water.
###

What are the skincare benefits of oat?

Image: aveen woman back 1 
Aveeno harnesses the power of the oat through many ways:

Oat Extract/Oat Essence (liquid produced from the oat plant) is naturally rich in Avenanthramides, which are known for their soothing and potent antioxidant properties.

Colloidal Oatmeal (a powder produced by the fine grinding of oats) has moisturising properties that help prevent water loss from the skin.
Oat Oil (a liquid extracted from oat grain) is naturally rich in lips which are essential components for a proper functioning skin barrier.
###

Is AVEENO ® suitable for eczema-prone skin?

Our Dermexa Range is formulated for very dry itchy skin, and is also suitable for eczema- prone skin.

What are prebiotics and probiotics?

Although they sound pretty similar, probiotics and prebiotics are two vastly different things with specific functions. Probiotics are living microorganisms that are found both naturally in your body and in food and supplements. When consumed or applied to the skin, they provide a wealth of positive benefits for the body, including:

  * Promoting good gut health

  * Strengthening skin overall
Prebiotics on the other hand aren’t actually alive. They are non-digestible ingredients that help to nourish the good bacteria in your gut or on your skin and balance the microbiome.

When probiotics and prebiotics are combined, whether that be in skin cream or in foods, they join forces to become what’s known as a synbiotic. Common synbiotics include supplements, additives and certain foods like yoghurt and cheese.
###

What is the skin microbiome?

Your skin’s microbiome is the collective name for the ecosystem of tiny microorganisms that live on and beneath the surface of your skin. It’s made up of a diverse range of different organisms playing different roles, including:

  * Bacteria – A variety of microscopic organisms which can be both potentially harmful and beneficial to the health of your skin

  * Fungi – Microbes that can be harmful or helpful, a heavy build-up can cause fungal infections
  * Mites – Insect-like microorganisms, invisible to the human eye, that can cause irritation in large numbers

  * Viruses – Microscopic molecules that, if allowed to multiply, can cause infection or illness on the skin
###

Is Aveeno gluten free?

###

What is Aveeno Skin Renewal?

The Aveeno^{®} Skin Renewal Body Range has been formulated to address rough & bumpy skin, uneven tone and loss of firmness concerns. Even more importantly, the products are formulated for sensitive skin.
The range comprising of a Gentle Scrub , Smoothing Cream and Firming Lotion is formulated with nourishing oat known to help support the microbiome and naturally derived PHA: a combination of ingredients selected specifically with sensitive skin in mind. The naturally derived PHA was selected due to its larger molecule size, which doesn’t penetrate the skin as deeply & is therefore more suitable for sensitive skin than other skincare acid groups (AHA’s, BHA’s).
###

Who is Aveeno Skin Renewal for?

The Aveeno Skin Renewal range is formulated for those with dry, sensitive skin. There are three products in the range with different benefits:

  * •Gentle Body Scrub: A precursor to either the Smoothing Cream or Firming Lotion. Formulated with prebiotic oat + niacinamide + naturally derived PHA to get rid of dead skin build-up. Helping to boost skin's natural renewal process through gentle exfoliation. Ensuring skin is ready for smoothing or firming.
  * •Smoothing Cream: Formulated with prebiotic oat + niacinamide + naturally derived PHA to leave dry, rough & bumpy skin feeling smoothed, soft and moisturised in just one night. Also suitable for people with Keratosis Pilaris
  * •Firming Lotion: clinically-proven to moisturise and improve skin elasticity in dry, unfirm and uneven skin. As well as nourishing oat and naturally derived PHA, it contains blackberry leaf extract, known to help enhance collagen and elastin recovery, and can help protect against premature ageing.
###

What is PHA? Are PHA’s good for the skin

Polyhydroxy acids (PHAs) are a popular skincare ingredient that have a wide range of benefits including moisturisation, renewal, and  can enhace stratum corneum barrier function . PHAs can also be better for sensitive skin than other commonly used chemical exfoliants, such as AHAS and BHAs, as they have a larger molecular structure so don’t penetrate as deeply into the skin.

For more information on PHAs see here ###

What other key ingredients are in skin renewal

All three products in the range contain both Nourishing Oat & Naturally Derived PHA to help support the skins microbiome and promote skin renewal for improved tone & texture.

Both the Gentle Body Scrub & Smoothing Cream also contain niacinamide which is known to help brighten skin & reduce discoloration. Whilst the Gentle Body Scrub also contains naturally derived beads, and helps promote skin cell turnover.
The Firming Lotion contains Blackberry Leaf Extract known to help enhance collagen & elastin recovery.
###

Is Skin Renewal suitable for sensitive skin?

Skin Renewal is formulated for sensitive skin. Featuring both nourishing oat & naturally derived PHA. Ingredients known to be gentler on sensitive skin types. Read more about PHA here .

###

Is Skin Renewal dermatologist tested?

All three products in the Skin Renewal range are dermatologist tested.
###

How often should I use skin renewal?

The Gentle Body Scrub can be used 1-2 times per week and can be incorporated into usual shower or bath regime. The Smoothing Cream or Firming Lotion can be used daily to help smooth, moisturise or firm skin.
###

How to apply skin renewal?

 Gentle Body Scrub

Apply a generous amount onto dry or damp skin and massage in circular motions, paying particular attention to dry and rough areas such as elbows, knees and heels. Rinse off with water. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.

 Smoothing Cream

Apply liberally all over body to leave your skin feeling smooth & moisturised. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.

 Firming Lotion
Use daily to moisturise & visibly firm. Do not use on irritated skin. Stop use if irritation occurs.
###

Is Skin Renewal fragrance free?

All three Skin Renewal products are fragrance free.

Customer Service FAQs
Zyliss Guarantee FAQs
Is my Zyliss item covered by a guarantee? Yes, all Zyliss items come with a manufacturer's guarantee, which varies by product.
How long is the manufacturer's guarantee? Most Zyliss items are covered by at least a 5-year guarantee. Please check your product packaging or the manual for specific details.
How do I register my guarantee? There's no need to register your guarantee. However, please retain your original proof of purchase to validate any claims.
What does the guarantee cover? The guarantee covers manufacturer faults within the guarantee period only.
What is NOT covered under the guarantee? The guarantee does not cover accidental breakage, poor care, misuse, or dismantling. Rust, corrosion, and loss of blade sharpness are also not covered. We may request an inspection by our Quality Team to confirm eligibility.
How do I make a guarantee claim? To initiate a claim under the Zyliss manufacturer guarantee, please contact us with detailed information and relevant images to support your claim.
My product is faulty, what do I do? If purchased within 6 months, please contact the retailer. For items older than 6 months, your consumer rights are with us, the manufacturer.
Zyliss Web Order Questions
Can I purchase a product from Zyliss by phone or mail-order? We only accept orders through our website at zyliss.co.uk due to our payment security policy.
How do I exchange/return a product? Please email us at contact.uk@dkhouseholdbrands.com with your name, order number, and intention.
Can I buy a gift voucher? Yes, gift vouchers are available and can be purchased here.
Product FAQs
Where are your items made? Our Zyliss products are manufactured in China.
At what temperature are my nylon and silicone tools heat resistant? Both nylon and silicone utensils are heat resistant up to 200°C.
Is Zyliss product packaging recyclable? Most of our packaging is made from recyclable materials. Look for the recycling logo on the packaging.
Is Zyliss.co.uk order packaging recyclable? Yes, we use plastic-free packaging, including cardboard boxes and paper void-fill, which are recyclable in most household waste recycle bins.
Have Zyliss products won any awards? Yes, several Zyliss products have won the Red Dot Award, including our Ice Cream Scoop and Gourmet Mandoline.
What is the Red Dot Award? The Red Dot Award is an internationally recognised accolade awarded for excellence in product design, communication design, and design concepts.
Are Zyliss products made from food-safe materials? Yes, all our products comply with EU regulations regarding food contact and safety, and are free from harmful substances like cadmium.
Can I put my Zyliss products in the dishwasher? Yes, our products are dishwasher safe unless stated otherwise. However, we recommend hand washing components with blades to maintain sharpness.
What is BPA? BPA (Bisphenol A) is a chemical used in making certain plastics and resins. All new Zyliss products are BPA-free.
What is the Zyliss limited lifetime warranty? The Zyliss Cook Ceramic Pan comes with a limited lifetime warranty covering material or workmanship defects. The non-stick coating is guaranteed for 2 years from the purchase date.
Additional Information
How can I place an order with Zyliss? Currently, we do not take orders over the phone, by email, or post. Please visit our online or in-store stockists to purchase Zyliss items.
I want to return something I purchased on Amazon. Can I send it back to you? Please return Amazon.co.uk purchases through your Amazon account. We cannot accept returns directly at Zyliss UK Head Office.
How long will it take to get my order? We ship orders within 2 business days. Most UK addresses receive their orders the next day, but please allow 3-5 days for delivery.
My purchase is a gift. Can you remove any receipts before sending? We do not include pricing or receipts in the box, making our orders suitable for gifting.
Can I add a gift message to the gift box? Currently, we do not offer a gift note service.
Do you offer a gift wrapping service? We do not offer gift wrapping at this time.
Do you deliver internationally? We do not offer international shipping from zyliss.co.uk. For international orders, please visit zyliss.com (USA) or zyliss.ch (Switzerland).

Sustainability is at the heart of our evolution. We are committed to preserving the quality and innovation that customers have trusted for decades while continuously integrating more eco-conscious materials, smarter designs, and sustainable packaging solutions.
a brand in transformation
for over 70 years, zyliss has been synonymous with kitchen innovation, creating iconic gadgets like the garlic press, onion chopper, and salad spinner. today, we are proud to be at the forefront of a new era for our brand – one that places timeless design, clever innovation, and sustainability at its core.
[image: A simple, stylized graphic of a wheat head with five teal leaves on each side, arranged symmetrically against a transparent background.]
by nature.
whenever we reduce virgin plastic use by up to 50%, replacing it with wheat straw material—a renewable byproduct of wheat processing.
by design.
we choose the right materials in the right places to ensure durability and reduce food waste, such as silicone edges that scrape every last bit from the pot.
by choice
we transition to eco-friendly packaging, replacing plastic components with recyclable alternatives like kraft paper and paper wires.
[image: A large, bold number 5 in light gray-green is centered inside a circle of the same color on a transparent background.]
by quality.
every non-electrical zyliss product comes with a 5 or 10-year guarantee because nothing is more sustainable than durability.
innovating with greener materials
we are constantly innovating to reduce our environmental footprint, carefully selecting materials that balance durability, performance, and sustainability. this is reflected in our material choices:
wheat straw material
various components, such as handles and lids, are interspersed with wheat straw material
this renewable raw material reduces the need for virgin plastics by up to 50%, percentages vary on the product to guarantee durability
readily available worldwide, it is leftover material after harvesting and processing wheat grains – that cannot be eaten by animals and would otherwise be agricultural waste
[image: Tall pine trees viewed from below, their trunks stretching upward toward a blue sky with scattered clouds, branches adorned with green needles, creating a sense of height and natural beauty.]
[image: Tall pine trees viewed from below, their trunks stretching upward toward a blue sky with scattered clouds, branches adorned with green needles, creating a sense of height and natural beauty.]
expanding our sustainable materials
our cutting boards are made from fsc-certified recycled wood fiber.
our ultimate pro ceramic pans feature recycled aluminum, providing customers with more sustainable cookware options.
we will continue testing and pioneering sustainable solutions—just as karl zysset, our founder, would have done.
[image: Three Zyliss knives in cardboard packaging are displayed vertically: a steak knife, a serrated paring knife, and an offset knife, each with a grey handle against a dark background.]
[image: Three Zyliss knives in cardboard packaging are displayed vertically: a steak knife, a serrated paring knife, and an offset knife, each with a grey handle against a dark background.]
sustainable packaging philosophy
as part of our sustainability principles, we are transitioning all packaging components to recycled or recyclable materials*.
plastic-free alternatives: replacing cable ties with paper wires, clear plastic bags with silk paper, and plastic inserts with cardboard to secure products.
eco-conscious printing: using water-based ink for a more environmentally friendly finish. no more shiny, unrecyclable varnishes.
eliminating compound materials: ensuring all packaging materials are easy to separate and recycle. simplifying components to make recycling effortless.
*only exception is where plastic is required for safety reasons, such as pet shrink wrap for securely sealing knives, blade guards, etc.
the journey continues
sustainability is not a destination but a continuous journey. at zyliss, we are committed to refining, innovating, and pushing boundaries to create a greener future. inspired by karl zysset’s pioneering spirit, we strive to make sustainability a seamless part of everyday cooking—without compromise.
